The accessible label defaults to `{count} new` and always reads the real count, never the capped text. Display-only, not a touch target                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Button`/`Card`/`Badge`/`Input`/`PasswordInput`/`EmptyState`/`ErrorState`/`ProgressBar`/`ProgressRing`/`SegmentedControl`/`Stepper`/`Text`/`NumericReturnBar`/`KeyboardAwareScrollView` | Pre-existing kit primitives — see the component source for each's own notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

**Failure-handling primitives (WP-02, audit §6.3 / §6.8)** — shared by mobile and web:

- **Default mutation-failure message.** `makeQueryClient` (mobile `src/lib/trpc.ts`, web `src/lib/trpc.ts`) installs a
  `MutationCache.onError` that shows `userFacingErrorMessage(error)` (mobile: snackbar via `showSnackbar`; web: `AppToastHost`
  mounted in `TRPCProvider`, `src/lib/app-toast.tsx`) unless the mutation carries `meta: { silent: true }` (typed through
  TanStack's `Register['mutationMeta']`), the error is a 401 (sign-out/redirect takes over) or an AI-consent refusal (the
  consent sheet reopens). Mutations that render their own error UI must pass `meta: { silent: true }`.
  Policy lives in `@chefer/utils` (`shouldNotifyMutationError`).
- **`userFacingErrorMessage`** (`@chefer/utils`) also maps a BAD_REQUEST whose message is Zod issue JSON to
  "Check the value you entered for <field>." (`weightKg` → "weight"); callers may pass `{ describeIssues }` for their own copy
  (gym limits). Never render `error.message` directly.
- **Query state.** `getQueryState` / `isNotFoundError` (`@chefer/utils`), `useQueryState` + `QueryStateView` (`@chefer/ui-mobile`),
  `useQueryState` (web `src/lib/use-query-state.ts`): `loading | error | empty | data`. A failed load renders `ErrorState` with
  Retry, never "Loading…" or "not found". `apps/mobile/tests/unit/query-state-grep.test.ts` fails on new `isLoading || !data`.
- **Notifications permission.** `useNotificationPermission()` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/`) returns `granted | denied | undetermined`
  and re-checks when the app returns to the foreground; `NotificationsOffRow` (`src/components/`) is the standard
  "Off for Chefer · Open Settings" row.
- **Confirms.** Two-button destructive confirms use `ConfirmSheet` (`busy` / `error`), not `Alert.alert`.

**Motion** (`src/motion/`, motion-system.md): `duration`/`springs`/`timing()` from `@chefer/tokens`,
`PressableScale` (MO-01), `haptics.*`, `useReducedMotion()`, `CountUp`, progress helpers. ui-mobile
has **no icon dependency** — pass an `Ionicons` (or other) node in; app-level features (e.g.
`apps/mobile/src/features/safety/*`, `.../premium/*`) import `@expo/vector-icons` directly.

**App-level pattern components** (not in the kit — feature folders, still part of the wave-0
pattern set): `apps/mobile/src/components/glossary-term.tsx` (**PAT-7** `GlossaryTerm` — inline
dotted-underline term that opens an `ExplainSheet`; presentational only, no `glossary.ts` import —
term/definition come in as props until that shared table lands); `apps/mobile/src/features/premium/`
`locked-feature-card.tsx` + `premium-sheet.tsx` (**PAT-3** UI shells — no wiring to real copy, the
nudge cap or the upgrade mutation); `apps/mobile/src/features/safety/filtered-for-line.tsx` +
`label-caveat.tsx` (**PAT-2** rows — "Filtered for … · n hidden", the compact/full label caveat);
`apps/mobile/src/features/gym/components/exercise-image.tsx` (**UX-05 A6, T-05.11** — `ExerciseImage`
`{ uri, equipment, size: 'thumb' | 'hero', hidden?, onImageFailed? }`: 3:2 always, `bg-muted` while
loading then MO-13 fade, one silent retry, the icon `Placeholder` — also exported — for a photo-less
exercise, a custom exercise, or one the photo audit hides. Wired into `photo-crossfade.tsx`
(exercise detail hero) so far; the other four surfaces the amendment lists (exercises-tab, the swap
picker, the workout card header, the technique sheet) still use their old image code — see
`mobile_parity_backlog.md`); `apps/mobile/src/components/swipe-to-remove.tsx` (**PAT-16, Δ2.6,
T-05.A1.2**) — `<SwipeToRemove onRemove testID?>`, RN core `PanResponder` driving a Reanimated
shared value (no `react-native-gesture-handler`, so no native rebuild). Claims the gesture only once
`shouldClaimSwipe(dx, dy)` sees clear horizontal intent (`|dx| > 12` and `|dx| > 2×|dy|`), so the
enclosing `ScrollView`'s vertical scroll is never fought; `shouldRemove(dx, rowWidth, vx)` decides a
release (35% of the row's width, or a fast flick) fires the same `onRemove` the `⋯`/long-press path
already calls — always progressive enhancement, never the only way to remove a set. Reduced motion
skips the fly-away tween and calls `onRemove` immediately. Wired onto the gym workout set row
(`apps/mobile/src/features/gym/workout/set-row.tsx`). `src/features/gym/library/{collapsible-chip-filters,use-keyboard-visible}.tsx`
(UX-05 A3 keyboard collapse) are also now built (A3.1, library sub-lane).

Tests: Jest + RNTL in `apps/mobile/tests/unit/` (`ui-*.test.tsx` for the kit, plus
`glossary-term.test.tsx`, `premium-shells.test.tsx`, `safety-shells.test.tsx`).

## 6. Database Schema

**Provider:** PostgreSQL 16
**ORM:** Prisma 5

### Entity Relationship Summary

```
User ─────────── UserProfile        (1:1, cascade delete)
User ─────────── Account[]          (1:N, cascade delete, OAuth)
User ─────────── Session[]          (1:N, cascade delete)
User ─────────── Post[]             (1:N, cascade delete)
User ─────────── ChefProfile        (1:1, cascade delete)
User ─────────── DietaryPreferences (1:1, cascade delete)
User ─────────── MealPlan[]         (1:N, cascade delete)
User ─────────── FavouriteRecipe[]  (1:N, cascade delete)
User ─────────── MealRating[]       (1:N, cascade delete)
User ─────────── ChefReview[]       (1:N, cascade delete, F1 weekly reviews)
User ─────────── HouseholdMember[]  (1:N, cascade delete, F2)
User ─────────── PantryItem[]       (1:N, cascade delete, F3)
User ─────────── EmailSend[]        (1:N, cascade delete, weekly-email send log, P2-5)
User ─────────── SafetyReport[]     (1:N, cascade delete, T-00.10 S3, §2.1)
User ─────────── TargetChange[]     (1:N, cascade delete, T-00.10 S12, §2.11)
User ─────────── ConsentEvent[]     (1:N, cascade delete, T-00.10 S14, append-only, §2.13)
MealPlan ──────── MealPlanDay[]     (1:N, cascade delete)
MealPlan ──────── MealPlanTailoring (1:0..1, cascade delete, premium live tailoring job)
                  MealPlan.isTemplate/name/isFollowed: week templates ("My weeks",
                  max 4/user, at most one followed) — excluded from every
                  week/active/history query; carry-forward clones the followed one
                  MealPlan.origin (MealPlanOrigin: USER | CARRY_FORWARD | TEMPLATE |
                  WEEKLY_AUTO): how the week came to exist — the Sunday worker only
                  replaces untouched CARRY_FORWARD copies; weekReady = WEEKLY_AUTO
Post ─────────── PostTag[]          (1:N, cascade delete)
Tag  ─────────── PostTag[]          (1:N, cascade delete)
PostTag          (composite PK: postId + tagId)
VerificationToken (standalone, password-reset tokens)
```

**MealPlanTailoring** (premium "instant week, then the chef tailors it live", 2026-09-28 — additive table + enum, `db push` safe)

| Field               | Type                    | Notes                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| id                  | String (cuid)           | PK                                                                                                             |
| planId              | String                  | FK → MealPlan, **unique**, cascade delete (deleting the plan deletes the job)                                  |
| userId              | String                  | Owner (plain column; indexed)                                                                                  |
| status              | MealPlanTailoringStatus | `RUNNING` / `DONE` / `PARTIAL` / `FAILED` / `CANCELLED` (superseded by a newer generation or plan not current) |
| totalDays           | Int                     | Days the job set out to tailor (planned days from today on)                                                    |
| queuedDays          | Int[]                   | Still to do, in order (today first; Monday first for a future week)                                            |
| tailoredDays        | Int[]                   | Replaced with an AI day                                                                                        |
| keptDays            | Int[]                   | Left alone — the user changed or logged them after generation                                                  |
| failedDays          | Int[]                   | The AI couldn't produce a usable day in budget — the curated day stays                                         |
| currentDay          | Int?                    | Being tailored now                                                                                             |
| snapshots           | Json                    | `{ "<dayOfWeek>": PlanMealSlotJson[] }` as generated — a mismatch means the user touched the day               |
| baselineCheckedKeys | String[]                | Shopping ticks at queue time; a new tick stops the job                                                         |
| slotTypes           | String[]                | Meal types a tailored day may hold (plan shape at generation)                                                  |
| leftovers           | Boolean                 | Generated with "cook once, eat twice" (pairs are locked slots)                                                 |
| strikes             | Int                     | Consecutive failures; 3 stops the job                                                                          |
| resumes             | Int                     | `mealPlan.resumeTailoring` uses (max 3 per plan)                                                               |
| nextRunAt           | DateTime                | When the job is next due (capacity back-off pushes it out)                                                     |
| leaseUntil          | DateTime?               | Claim lease (150 s) — a crashed step's job is picked up again once it lapses                                   |
| lastError           | String?                 | Last failure / stop reason (diagnostics)                                                                       |
| createdAt/updatedAt | DateTime                | Auto-managed                                                                                                   |
| finishedAt          | DateTime?               | Set on DONE/PARTIAL/FAILED/CANCELLED                                                                           |

Indexes: `@@index([status, nextRunAt])` (the worker's claim query), `@@index([userId])`.
Repository: `mealPlanTailoringRepository` (`packages/database/src/repositories/meal-plan-tailoring.repository.ts`) — create/upsert, lease claim (`claimNextDue`, per-row `updateMany` guard like the image worker), `saveProgress` (releases the lease unless `keepLease`), `cancelRunningForWeek`, compare-and-set `replaceDayIfUnchanged` (serializable transaction: plan still ACTIVE and day JSON still equals the snapshot), plus the narrow reads the worker needs (`findCheckedKeys`, `findLoggedRecipeIds`, `findUserGate` = tier/role/`aiDataConsentAt`).

**Gym models** (gym_plan.md §2.2; schema from G0-2, repositories + services from G1-B). Weights are
kg (`Float`, 0.01 precision) rendered in `GymProfile.unit`. Ids a phone creates offline
(sessions, session exercises, sets) are **client UUIDs** so the sync upsert is idempotent.

| Model                 | Key / relations                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Exercise`            | `id` = curated slug or custom UUID; `ownerId?` → User (cascade)  | `ownerId = null` = curated, upserted from `@chefer/types` `EXERCISE_CATALOG` at API boot (`ensureExerciseLibrary`, `contentVersion` bumps on content change, dropped slugs archived). Custom rows are owner-only and archived, never deleted. `imageKeys` → `/static/exercises/<key>`. **S18 (T-42.0):** `trackingType ExerciseTrackingType` (default `WEIGHT_REPS`) says how the row logs (weight×reps, bodyweight reps, duration, duration+distance, distance, intervals); `isTimed` stays as the legacy mirror for old clients (`isTimedFor()`). Derive it defensively with `trackingTypeOf()` (`@chefer/utils` `gym/tracking.ts`) rather than reading the column raw, so a pre-backfill or pre-W2 cached row still resolves correctly |
| `GymProfile`          | `userId` PK → User (cascade)                                     | Setup answers + equipment inventory. JSON: `goalHistory` `[{ fromWeek (Monday), goal }]`; `offerState` (API-owned) `{ dismissed: {key→ISO}, deload: {startDate,endDate} \| null, knownWeightsKg: {exerciseId→kg} }`. **S21 (T-42.0):** `distanceUnit DistanceUnit?` — null = derived from `unit` (`MI` when `unit = LB`, else `KM`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Routine`             | `userId` → User; `days` RoutineDay[] (cascade)                   | One `isActive` per user. `version` = optimistic concurrency for document saves (bumped only by `routine.save`). `nextDayId` = rotation pointer (NOT document content; moved by completed sessions and `setNextDay`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `RoutineDay`          | `routineId` (cascade); `exercises` RoutineExercise[] (cascade)   | `position`, `plannedWeekday` 0 = Mon … 6 = Sun                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `RoutineExercise`     | `dayId` (cascade); `exerciseId` → Exercise                       | A slot: sets, rep range, target RIR, rest, superset group. Ids survive document saves when the client sends them back                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `WorkoutSession`      | `id` client UUID; `userId` → User                                | Full synced document. `clientUpdatedAt` = last-write-wins guard; `rotationAppliedAt` = set once when completion advanced `Routine.nextDayId` (re-syncs never advance twice). `localDate` is the device's date                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `SessionExercise`     | `id` client UUID; `sessionId` (cascade); `exerciseId` → Exercise | Snapshot of the slot at start + `prescription` JSON (the engine Suggestion shown) + nullable `supersetGroup` (this session's superset letter, 2026-10); deleted + recreated on every applied upsert                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `SessionSet`          | `id` client UUID; `sessionExerciseId` (cascade)                  | `completedAt null` = planned, not ticked. **S20 (T-42.0):** `+ durationSec Int?`, `+ distanceM Float?` (canonical metres), `+ intensityRpe Int? (1–10)`, `+ resistanceLevel Int?`, `+ inclinePct Float?`, `+ caloriesKcal Float?`, `+ avgHeartRateBpm Int?` (reserved, never written from manual entry) — all null for a strength set; a cardio entry is ONE row (`weightKg: 0, reps: 0, isWarmup: false`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ExerciseProgression` | PK `[userId, exerciseId, repBucket]`                             | **Derived cache**: `state` is recomputed by folding the engine over completed sessions (`ProgressionService.recompute`). `override` (user-edited next targets) survives recomputes and is cleared once an exposure newer than it is logged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `TrainingPause`       | `userId` → User                                                  | Inclusive localDate range that freezes the streak (≤ 35 days, no overlaps)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

```prisma

                           TREADMILL  BIKE  ROWER  ELLIPTICAL  STAIR_CLIMBER  SKI_ERG  ASSAULT_BIKE  JUMP_ROPE  POOL  OUTDOOR }  // S19 (T-42.0, 06 §5.3) — cardio equipment, never sent to a client below API level 3

enum WorkoutStatus      { IN_PROGRESS  COMPLETED  DISCARDED }
// S18 (T-42.0) — cardio-as-first-class-type (UX-42). INTERVALS unused until W5.
enum ExerciseTrackingType { WEIGHT_REPS  BODYWEIGHT_REPS  DURATION  DURATION_DISTANCE  DISTANCE  INTERVALS }
enum DistanceUnit         { KM  MI }  // S21 (T-42.0) — GymProfile.distanceUnit
```

### Data fix `scripts/data-fixes/2026-10-03-two-of-us-eater-portion.sql` (UX-PLAN-02)

No schema change, and not a Prisma migration (deploys use `prisma db push`, which never applies migration files): the owner runs it by hand once after the WP-01 deploy. A one-off, idempotent `UPDATE` on `meal_plan_days.meals`: for users whose `dietary_preferences.cookingFor = 2`, a slot with `portion` exactly 2 (the old "two of us" table override) loses the key, i.e. becomes the eater's 1×. Other slots and users are untouched. "Two of us" now scales Shop/cost/cook at read time instead of the stored portion.

### Wave-2 cardio catalogue + server delivery (T-42.1/T-42.2, L-GYM)

12 cardio catalogue entries (06 §6, `DURATION`/`DURATION_DISTANCE` only — the other 18 + every `INTERVALS` entry land
in W5's T-42.6): `treadmill-walk`, `treadmill-incline-walk`, `treadmill-run`, `outdoor-walk`, `outdoor-run`,
`outdoor-cycle`, `stationary-bike-upright`, `stationary-bike-recumbent`, `spin-class`, `elliptical`,
`rowing-machine`, `stair-climber`. Built by a new `cardio()` structural builder beside `ex()`
(`packages/types/src/gym/exercise-catalog.ts`) — `loadType: 'WEIGHTED'` (not `'BODYWEIGHT'`: the catalog invariant
test ties `loadType: 'BODYWEIGHT'` to `equipment: 'BODYWEIGHT'`), empty muscle lists (cardio earns no fractional set
in `volumeByGroup`), `repMin/repMax/restSec/incrementKg` unused placeholders. MET ranges, `metrics` shown per entry
and the rower's metres-not-km/mi distance flag live in **NEW** `packages/types/src/gym/cardio-catalog.ts`
(`CARDIO_CATALOG`, `CARDIO_CATALOG_BY_ID`, `CARDIO_EXERCISE_IDS`). `apps/api/src/lib/exercise-library/ensure.ts`'s
`catalogToWriteData` now writes `trackingType` — only when the catalogue entry sets it explicitly (the `cardio()`
rows), so `changedFields()` never diffs it for the other ~79 entries and the boot backfill stays the only thing that
derives one for them.

**Server delivery (Δ2.1's filter, wired for real).** `apps/api/src/application/gym/client-level.ts` gained
`filterExerciseDtosForLevel()` and `filterSessionExercisesForLevel()`, applied in the four read paths the plan calls
out: `gym.bootstrap` (`library` + each `recentSessions` entry's `exercises`), `gym.library.list`,
`gym.session.get`, `gym.session.list` — every one now threads `ctx.clientApiLevel` from its router down to the
service. A session's exercises are filtered in place (built from a `trackingTypeById` map: bootstrap already has the
user's exercise rows loaded; `session.get`/`.list` fetch it via `exerciseRepo.findVisibleByIds`) — the session
itself is never dropped, so week counts and streaks are unaffected for an old client. `mappers.ts`'s `toExerciseMeta`
now sets `trackingType` (always present — the DB column defaults `WEIGHT_REPS`), `toProfileDto` now sets
`distanceUnit`, and `toSessionDoc`'s set mapping now carries the seven S20 fields (`?? undefined`, so a strength set
round-trips without gaining `null`-valued keys an old client has never seen). `workout-session.service.ts`'s
`toWriteData` mirrors this the other way (`?? null`) so a cardio set's fields actually persist — previously
`mappers.ts`/`toWriteData` didn't map them at all, so nothing cardio-shaped ever reached the database. `gym-profile
.service.ts`'s `completeSetup` and its router now also pass the level through to the bootstrap it returns.
`progression.service.ts`'s `recompute`/`forExercises` skip any exercise whose `trackingTypeOf()` isn't a strength
type — Δ2.2: cardio has no stored progression state; PR/e1RM/volume code needed no equivalent change, since a
cardio `SessionSet` (`weightKg: 0, reps: 0`) already produces nothing in `bestE1rm`/`kindsBeaten`/`groupShare`.
`gym-export.service.ts`'s CSV gained `Duration (s)`, `Distance (m)`, `Effort (RPE)` columns (blank for a strength
row). New flag `cardioLogging` (`packages/types/src/feature-flags.ts`), off by default (Q-24).
`packages/types/src/gym/dto.ts`'s `SessionSummaryDto['exercises'][number]['sets']` also gained the same seven S20
fields (additive/optional; `toSessionSummary`, `packages/utils/src/gym/session.ts`, maps them) so
`bootstrap.recentSessions`/`gym.session.list` can show cardio history without shipping the full `WorkoutSessionDoc`.

**Cardio is level 3, not 2** — see the §9 note. `renderableTrackingTypes(level >= 3)` is what actually gates all of
the above; nothing here is reachable below level 3 regardless of `cardioLogging`.

Contract test **NEW** `apps/mobile/tests/contract/gym-cardio.contract.test.ts` pins AC10 (a level-0/1/2 —
including the live App Store build — `gym.bootstrap`/`gym.library.list` contains no cardio row) plus level-3
round-tripping, a mixed session dropping only its cardio exercise for an old reader, and `progression.recompute`
never creating a row for a cardio exercise.

### Following (friends) schema (F0.1, additive only)

Code name `friends`, user-facing name **Following** (`docs/friends/implementation-plan.md` §2). One additive migration
(`packages/database/prisma/migrations/20260930120000_friends_schema/`): new enums, seven new tables, four nullable
`recipes` columns and one new `ConsentKind` value. Nothing is renamed or removed, so installed app binaries keep
working. Production applies it with `prisma db push --skip-generate` (no `--accept-data-loss`).

**New enums:** `ProfileVisibility` (`PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`), `FollowStatus` (`PENDING`, `ACCEPTED`), `NotificationKind`
(`FOLLOW_REQUEST`, `NEW_FOLLOWER`, `REQUEST_ACCEPTED`), `ReportReason` (`INAPPROPRIATE`, `SPAM`, `HARASSMENT`, `UNSAFE`,
`OTHER`), `RecipeHiddenReason` (`REPORTS`, `FILTER`), `ModerationAction` (`RECIPE_AUTO_HIDDEN`, `ACCOUNT_FORCED_PRIVATE`,
`RECIPE_FILTER_HIDDEN`, `NAME_REJECTED`, `RECIPE_TEXT_REJECTED`, `UNDO`). **Added value:** `ConsentKind.SOCIAL_SHARING`
(turn-on, visibility and targets-sharing consent; withdrawn on Turn off).

**New models** (all cascade from `User`; repositories in §5.1):

| Model (table)                                   | Key / relations                                                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SocialProfile` (`social_profiles`)             | PK `userId` → User (cascade)                                                                    | One row = the user turned Following on; no row = not discoverable, not followable. `visibility` (default `PRIVATE`), `searchName` (`normalizeSearchName()`), `sharePlan`/`shareRecipes`/`shareWorkouts` (default `true`), `shareTargets` (default `false`), `forcedPrivateAt` (moderation lock), `featured` (Chefer Kitchen), `activatedAt`, `updatedAt`. Indexes `[visibility, forcedPrivateAt]`, `[searchName]` |
| `Follow` (`follows`)                            | `followerId`, `followeeId` → User (cascade, relations `FollowsOut`/`FollowsIn`)                 | Directed edge; `status` `PENDING` = request, `acceptedAt`. `@@unique([followerId, followeeId])`; indexes `[followeeId, status, createdAt]`, `[followerId, status, createdAt]`. Decline / cancel / unfollow / remove / block = delete the row                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Block` (`blocks`)                              | PK `[blockerId, blockedId]` → User (cascade)                                                    | Index `[blockedId]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `SuggestionDismissal` (`suggestion_dismissals`) | PK `[userId, dismissedUserId]` → User (cascade)                                                 | "Not interested" on a suggestion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `UserReport` (`user_reports`)                   | `reporterId`, `targetUserId` → User (cascade); `recipeId` is a plain column, **no FK**          | Append-only. `reason ReportReason`, `eligible` (reporter account >= 24 h old and email verified, evaluated at report time), `discountedAt` (set by an ops undo; discounted reports never count again). Indexes `[targetUserId, eligible]`, `[recipeId, eligible]`, `[createdAt]`                                                                                                                                  |
| `ModerationLog` (`moderation_log`)              | `targetUserId` → User (cascade)                                                                 | Append-only log of every automatic moderation action and every ops undo: `action`, `recipeId?`, `reason`, `distinctReporters?`, `actor` (`system` \| `ops`), `undoOfId?`. Indexes `[createdAt]`, `[targetUserId]`                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Notification` (`notifications`)                | `userId` (recipient) and `actorId` → User (cascade, relations `NotificationsReceived`/`Caused`) | In-app Activity only (no push, no email). `kind`, `readAt?`. `@@unique([userId, kind, actorId])`: a re-sent request upserts (fresh `createdAt`, `readAt = null`). Indexes `[userId, createdAt]`, `[userId, readAt]`                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**`Recipe` additions** (all nullable, no backfill): `originRecipeId` and `originCreatorId` (set on a viewer's private
copy made by "Add to my week"; self-relations `RecipeCopies` and `RecipeOriginCreator`, both `onDelete: SetNull`, so
deleting an original or its creator leaves copies standing and orphaned), `hiddenAt` and `hiddenReason
RecipeHiddenReason?` (automatic moderation: hidden from everyone but the creator; existing hearts and copies keep
working). New indexes `[creatorId, originRecipeId]` and `[creatorId, source, createdAt]`. `User` gains the matching
back-relations (`socialProfile`, `followsOut`/`followsIn`, `blocksMade`/`blocksReceived`, `dismissalsMade`/
`dismissalsReceived`, `reportsMade`/`reportsReceived`, `moderationLog`, `notificationsReceived`/`notificationsCaused`,
`copiedRecipesOrigin`).

**Deviation from the plan (rev 2.1):** copy uniqueness on `[creatorId, originRecipeId]` is an `@@index`, **not** an
`@@unique`. Adding a unique constraint to the populated `recipes` table makes `prisma db push` stop with a data-loss
warning, and production's compose `migrate` service runs it without `--accept-data-loss`, which would block the deploy.
`RecipeCopyService` enforces "at most one copy per viewer and source" instead, with a SERIALIZABLE find-or-create and a
retry on `P2034`.

**Turning Following off vs deleting the account.** Turn off runs
`SocialProfileRepository.deleteCascadeSocial` in one transaction: it deletes the user's `SocialProfile`, `Follow`,
`Block`, `SuggestionDismissal` and `Notification` rows, but **keeps `UserReport` and `ModerationLog`**, so leaving and
re-joining cannot reset moderation. **Account deletion** cascades everything, including reports and the moderation log,
because every new table has `onDelete: Cascade` from `User` (`account-data.service.ts` needs no explicit step). The
`recipes.originRecipeId` / `originCreatorId` links on other people's copies go to `NULL`.

### Recipe soft delete (UX-REC-04, additive only)

One nullable column: `Recipe.deletedAt DateTime?` (null = live). `recipe.deleteMine` sets it on the caller's own
MANUAL recipe, `recipe.restoreMine` clears it (the Undo). Production applies it with `prisma db push --skip-generate`
(no data-loss prompt: a new nullable column); the named migration
`packages/database/prisma/migrations/20261003100000_recipe_deleted_at/` keeps the history honest. Nothing is
removed, so installed app binaries keep working.

Where a deleted recipe is **hidden** (`FavouriteRecipeRepository`, `FriendRecipeRepository`): every `recipe.list`
branch (All, Saved, Mine), a user's favourites and "use in next plan" pins, `findManualRecipeById` (so `getMyRecipe`,
`update` and the owner's `canEdit` stop at once), the copy lookup of `findOrCreateCopy`, and the Following shared-recipes
list. Deleting also removes the owner's own favourite row. Where it is **kept**: a plan slot that still holds the id
keeps resolving the row (`MealPlanRepository.findRecipesByIds` is untouched), so a plan never breaks; the recipe is
a tombstone there. `findRecipeVisibleTo` (`recipe-access.ts`) opens a deleted recipe only when it sits in one of the
caller's plans, which is what makes `mealPlan.getRecipe` answer with `deleted: true` for an old client's deep link and
`NOT_FOUND` (never a 500) everywhere else. `recipe.list` strips the raw column like the other Following columns.

### Ingredient catalog schema (P1 of `docs/plan-ingredient-catalog.md`, additive only)

The schema that lets a recipe's nutrition be **computed** from catalog ingredients × quantities (plan §3). Everything is
additive: nothing is renamed or removed, `IngredientPrice` keeps its name (a rename under `db push` is a drop), and
installed app binaries keep reading `Recipe.ingredients` / `nutritionInfo` unchanged. Production applies it with
`prisma db push --skip-generate` (verified on a dev clone: no data-loss prompt). A named migration
(`packages/database/prisma/migrations/20261001160000_ingredient_catalog/`) keeps the history honest.

**New enums:** `IngredientStatus` (`ACTIVE`, `MERGED`, `DEPRECATED`), `NutritionSource` (`USDA_FDC`, `CIQUAL`, `LABEL`,
`USER`, `ADMIN`; never an LLM), `NutritionStatus` (`COMPUTED`, `PARTIAL`, `USER_ENTERED`), `IngredientCategory` (36
values, plan §4.2). `@chefer/types` `nutrition.ts` mirrors them as string unions; `apps/api/src/lib/nutrition-contract.test.ts`
fails on drift.

| Model (table)                               | Key / relations                                                                                                                                               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Ingredient` (`ingredients`)                | cuid PK; `ownerId` → User (cascade; null = global); `mergedIntoId` → Ingredient (self, SetNull, relation `IngredientMerges`)                                  | `slug`, display `name`, `category`, `status`. Per-100 g edible nutrition, EU convention (carbs exclude fiber, D2): `kcal/protein/carbs/fat/fiberPer100g` required, `sugar/satFat/sodiumMgPer100g` optional. `densityGPerMl?`, `edibleFraction` (default 1). Provenance `nutritionSource`, `sourceRef` (`fdc:…`, `ciqual:…`, `label:…`), `sourceNote`. `@@unique([ownerId, slug])` |
| `IngredientAlias` (`ingredient_aliases`)    | → Ingredient (cascade)                                                                                                                                        | Normalized lookup key → ingredient; `locale` `en`/`ro`; `ownerId` null for global aliases. `@@unique([ownerId, alias])`, index `[alias]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `IngredientPortion` (`ingredient_portions`) | → Ingredient (cascade)                                                                                                                                        | Count/household unit → edible grams for ONE unit (`clove`, `medium`, `can`, …), `source` (`fdc-portion:…`, `label`, `admin`, `user`). `@@unique([ingredientId, unit])`                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `IngredientNotice` (`ingredient_notices`)   | `userId` → User (cascade)                                                                                                                                     | Weekly-review in-app notice (plan §8.2, D6): `kind` (`IngredientNoticeKind`: `VERIFIED_DATA` \| `CHECK_DATA`), `review` (date string), `ingredientNames String[]`, `readAt?`. `@@unique([userId, kind, review])`: re-applying a review refreshes the row                                                                                                                          |
| `RecipeIngredient` (`recipe_ingredients`)   | `recipeId` → Recipe (cascade); `ingredientId` → Ingredient (**SetNull**, so an account deletion that cascades a private row unlinks lines instead of failing) | One recipe line: `position`, `rawName` (never lost), `quantity`, canonical `unit`, resolved edible `grams` (null ⇒ unresolved), `note` (prep text), `optional` (excluded from totals). Indexes `[recipeId]`, `[ingredientId]`                                                                                                                                                     |

**`Recipe` additions:** `nutritionStatus` (default `PARTIAL`: every recipe is PARTIAL until the §7 migration writes its
lines), `nutritionComputedAt?`, `nutritionTotal Json?` (whole-recipe totals, same shape as `nutritionInfo`), back-relation
`lines`. `Recipe.ingredients` (Json) stays as the `{name, quantity, unit}` **mirror** of `lines`;
`RecipeLineRepository.writeLines` (§5.1) is the one path that writes rows, mirror and nutrition together.
**`IngredientPrice` addition:** nullable `ingredientId` → Ingredient (SetNull, indexed). Its macro columns are now
deprecated: no new code reads them. **`User` addition:** back-relation `privateIngredients`.

**Global slug and alias uniqueness (decision for plan §3's NULL note).** Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so
`@@unique([ownerId, slug])` and `@@unique([ownerId, alias])` do not stop two **global** rows sharing a slug or alias.
Storing `""` for globals would break the `ownerId` foreign key, and Prisma 5 can express neither partial indexes nor
`NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (and `db push` drops indexes it does not know). So global uniqueness is enforced where global rows
are written: by the catalog validators (CI) and by `ingredients:sync`, the only writer of global rows (D7).

## 7. API Layer

### Layered Architecture

```
Router (tRPC)          ← thin, only input/output + auth guard
  └── Service          ← business logic, orchestrates repos
        └── Repository ← data access (Prisma), behind interface
              └── Prisma Client
```

### UserService (application layer)

Wraps `IUserRepository`. Methods: `findById`, `findByEmail`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `delete`.
Maps domain errors (e.g., `UserNotFoundError`) to tRPC error codes.

### PreferencesService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/preferences/preferences.service.ts`. Methods: `hasProfile` (goal set), `get` (reports `dietaryPreferences.servingSize` derived from the household via an injected `HouseholdPort`, P2-3; additive `jobs: OnboardingJob[]` via `effectiveJobs()`, §2.4, T-03.1), `setIntent` (onboarding audience, every tier; rev 2 also back-fills `onboardingJobs` when never answered), `setJobs` (§2.4, T-03.1 — jobs + optional `trainingWeekdays`/`autoPlanWeekly`, writes the legacy intent via `legacyIntentForJobs()`), `setHomeDisplay` (§2.4, T-04.1 — the explicit "show nutrition on Today" override), `setDisplayPreferences` (units + currency + `timeZone` — §2.12, T-21.1: the IANA name server-initiated work reads, every tier; syncs the gym unit through an injected `GymUnitSync`, lazily wired to `gymProfileService.syncFromPreferredUnits` so the service never loads the gym graph eagerly — P2-6), `setup` (never shrinks the safety lists — it unions saved and submitted allergies/restrictions/dislikes, since the onboarding wizard can be re-opened after an upgrade; F-ONB-1-1), `update` (backing `preferences.updateSafety`, `preferences.updateTargets` and the every-tier `preferences.saveProfileBasics` — the split is enforced at the router's auth level, P1-2 / ux-fixes-plan.md 3.1), `setAutoPlanWeekly` (§2.13, T-39.2: after the profile write succeeds, calls `consentService.record({ kind: 'AUTO_PLAN', granted, source: 'web'|'mobile' })` — the source is `ctx.isMobileClient` at the router).
A `servingSize > 1` written by an older app build (setup/updateTargets) is absorbed into the household right after the write (`HouseholdPort.migrateLegacyServingSize`). Orchestrates `IChefProfileRepository` + `IDietaryPreferencesRepository` inside a Prisma `$transaction`. Recomputes `dailyCalorieTarget` via Mifflin-St Jeor on every update. Accepts `deliveryAddress` and `deliveryCurrency` fields.

**`resolveTargets(profile, lifterBodyweightKg?)`** (§2.11, T-35.1) — THE single resolver, returning `{ effective, suggested, source: 'own'|'suggested', inputs }`. `suggested` is the existing computation (live Mifflin-St Jeor TDEE ± goal adjustment ± the coach's `targetAdjustmentKcal` dial, macros from the goal's split, lifter g/kg protein + the BMI ≥ 30 adjusted-weight rule when a lifter bodyweight is passed — `packages/utils/training-nutrition.ts`'s `withLifterProteinDetailed`). `effective` is the user's own numbers when `ChefProfile.targetMode === 'OWN'` (`customKcal`/`customProteinG`/`customCarbsG`/`customFatG`, falling back per-field to `suggested`) — a gym-setup change, a new weigh-in or a goal edit only ever move `suggested`, never `effective` (AC2). `inputs` are the values `packages/utils/explain-targets.ts`'s sentences name. **`resolveDailyTargets(profile, lifterBodyweightKg?)`** is now a thin wrapper returning `resolveTargets(...).effective` — every existing consumer (dashboard, tracker, meal-plan generation, the coach review, `TrainingNutritionService`) picks up the own-target override and the `RECOMP`/`PERFORMANCE` goals with zero call-site changes.

### CoachService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/coach/coach.service.ts` (F1 Adaptive Chef). The Sunday review loop:
`runReviewSweep` (called by WeeklyPlanWorker BEFORE plan generation) finds users with ≥3 logged
days in the closing week and writes one `ChefReview` row per user-week, idempotently
(`@@unique(userId, weekStart)`, weekStart = UTC Monday midnight). Metrics and the adjustment
policy live in the PURE module `application/coach/review.service.ts` (adherence, avg kcal,
EWMA α=0.25 weight trend over `WeightEntry` rows; LOSE plateau ×2 consecutive → −100 kcal
floored at BMR×1.1, GAIN stall → +100 kcal ceilinged at TDEE+500, adherence <50% → no change).
**§2.11, T-35.4 (rev 2): the coach proposes, it never writes `ChefProfile.targetAdjustmentKcal` itself any more.** The computed adjustment is stored on `ChefReview.proposedAdjustmentKcal` and surfaced as a `SUGGESTED`/`COACH` `TargetChange` (`TargetsService.proposeCoachAdjustment`, best-effort — a failure there never loses the review); `ChefReview.adjustmentKcal` keeps meaning "applied" and stays 0 until the user accepts via `targets.acknowledgeChange({ keep: false })` (which then bumps the dial that `resolveTargets` applies AFTER the goal adjustment and BEFORE the protein cap). Free-tier reviews are written teaser-only (nothing proposed). Review prose (`buildTemplateReviewText`) says "I'd suggest moving next week's calorie budget by…", never "I've adjusted…" — old clients' banners stay true. Review prose comes from `application/coach/review-text.ts` via
`IAIService.generateReviewText` (primary-first with failover like other generation calls;
non-medical tone rules in `lib/ai/prompts.ts`; deterministic template in mock mode or on failure).
`getCurrentReview` shapes the payload by entitlement: full for `adaptiveCoaching`, first-line
teaser for free (the full text never leaves the server). Targets come from
`resolveDailyTargets(profile, lifterBodyweightKg)`: lifters are judged on their g/kg protein rule,
and the review adds one protein line (average logged protein vs target; template + AI prompt
field `protein`) for lifters only. Depends on `IChefReviewRepository`,
`IChefProfileRepository`, `IWeightEntryRepository` and `TrainingNutritionService.loadLifter`
(constructor-injected for tests).

### HouseholdService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/household/household.service.ts` (F2 "Feed the Whole Table", premium_plan.md W2-D; free member safety + one people model since backlog P2-3). CRUD over `IHouseholdMemberRepository` (constructor-injected): `list` (converts a legacy servingSize first), `add` (capped by `getLimit(user, 'householdMembers')` — **5 on both tiers**; count + insert run in one SERIALIZABLE transaction with P2034 retry via `createWithinCap`, so parallel adds can't pass the cap — F-ONB-3-1), `update`/`remove` (ownership-scoped, NOT_FOUND otherwise), `scalingPortions(user)` (the table's portion sum when the user has `householdPlans` AND members, else null — the one scaling decision the shopping list uses), `migrateLegacyServingSize(userId)` (best effort) and `backfillLegacyServingSizes()` (run once at API boot). Also exports the PURE helpers:

- `scalingTable(user)` / `tableFor(userId, members)` (UX-PLAN-02, UX-REC-02) — who the list/cost/pantry are cooked for: `{ members, cookingFor }` (members only for premium scaling, plus the "How you cook" setting via `PlanShapeService`), or null. Feeds `slotShopFactor` (`application/shared/household-scale.ts`) → `portionsFor` (`@chefer/utils`): quantity = recipe line × (slot eater portion + Σ members | cookingFor − 1) [÷ recipe.servings for a members table]. `scalingPortions` stays for the response's `portions` field.
- `legacyServingSizePlaceholders(n)` — servingSize N → N−1 standard-portion `Person 2…N` members (capped at 5); deterministic. The repository's `migrateLegacyServingSize` claims the value with a conditional `UPDATE … WHERE servingSize = N` (reset to 1) and inserts the placeholders in the same transaction only when the user has no members, so it is idempotent and race-safe.
- `derivedServingSize(members)` — the legacy field old app builds read: `min(6, householdPortionSum)`.

- `mergeHouseholdSafety(owner, members)` — case-insensitive union of every member's allergies + dietary restrictions with the owner's (SafetyPrefs shape; member dislikes stay OUT — they are soft). **Safety is never premium**: MealPlanService applies this union on the free curated path, curated swaps and AI swaps whenever members exist (e.g. created before a downgrade).
- `computeHouseholdContext(members, owner)` — fills `MealPlanInput.householdContext`: `portionSum = householdPortionSum(members)` from `@chefer/utils` (`ceil(1 owner portion + Σ member portionFactor)`; drives recipe servings + quantity scaling, and premium generation's `servingSize` — the legacy setting is no longer read), `mergedSafety`, and per-member `dislikeNotes` ("avoid mushrooms for Maria"); `undefined` with no members so the seam stays absent.

### ChatService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/chat/chat.service.ts` (P1-4). Backs `POST /api/chat`: enforces the matrix chat quota (`chatMessagesPerDay` — FREE 5/day counted from `ai_call_logs` CHAT rows, premium unlimited), builds a fresh per-message context from the user's REAL data (today's meals with macros + day totals, weekly overview, resolved daily targets, allergies/restrictions/dislikes, recent rating signals) and hands the model tools over the real services: `swapMeal` (performs an actual plan swap through MealPlanService, respecting the swap quota; optional `occurrence` — 2 = the day's second snack — resolves to `swapRecipe`'s `slotIndex`), `scaleRecipe` (rescales ingredient quantities from the active plan), `addToShoppingList` (items land in the customItems overlay), `logMeal` (F4 "I ate this" — logs a manual custom entry into today's tracker via TrackerService, rebalance included) and `whatCanIMake` (F3 — pantry-coverage ranking via PantryService; free tier gets a teaser). The Gemini implementation runs a bounded function-calling loop and streams the final answer; the mock echoes the same context and exercises the same tool handlers. UX-FOOD-21: `buildTools` records a `ChatAction` per performed swap / shopping-list add / logged meal / import, and `chat(user, messages, { withActions })` appends them as a trailer (`withActionTrailer`) for an opted-in client; `customItemKey` (`shopping-list/custom-item-key.ts`) is shared so the shopping action reports the keys `shoppingList.removeCustomItem` needs for Undo.

### RecipeImportService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/recipe-import/recipe-import.service.ts` (F5 "Cheferize Anything", premium_plan.md W1-C). Backs `recipe.importPreview` / `recipe.importVideoPreview` / `recipe.importSave`:

- **`preview(user, source)`** — metered via `recipeImportsPerDay` (AiCallLog `RECIPE_IMPORT` rows, attempts not successes; FREE 1/day = the §6.4 ghost preview, premium 5/day). URL sources go through `lib/recipe-import/`: SSRF-guarded fetch (`ssrf-guard.ts` — http(s) only, default ports, every DNS-resolved address checked against private/loopback/link-local/metadata/CGNAT/ULA ranges; `fetch-page.ts` — 10 s timeout, 1 MB streaming cap, ≤3 redirects each re-validated) then a dependency-free readability strip (`extract-content.ts` — schema.org Recipe JSON-LD extraction, chrome/script removal, og:image, 20 k char cap). Extraction (`IAIService.extractRecipe`, text or photo multimodal) is followed by the **Cheferize pass** (`IAIService.cheferizeRecipe`: allergen/restriction substitutions, soft dislike swaps, serving rescale) whose output is **re-validated by the P1-2 allergen matcher — AI output is never trusted for safety**; surviving terms are reported and the adapted variant is unusable (fail closed).
  - **Nutrition is computed, never the AI's** (plan-ingredient-catalog §6.2, I2). Both variants' lines are resolved against the catalog (`IngredientResolver`, with fuzzy candidates) and computed by `RecipeNutritionService`. `original`/`adapted.nutritionInfo` carry the computed per-serving numbers.
  - Additive fields: `resolution.{original,adapted}[]` per line (`{ rawName, unit, note, confidence, match, candidates, grams, problem? }`, for the review form) and `nutritionStatus.{original,adapted}`.
  - `macroCheck` keeps its shape for installed clients but is derived from that computation: `ok` when every adapted line computes, `unknown` otherwise; stated calories = computed calories, so the old "uncertain" banner never shows. `crossCheckMacros` is deleted.
- **`previewVideo(user, url)`** (2026-09-26, owner decision "Gemini must go") — a video link becomes a **draft for the user to review**, not a Cheferize diff. Same `RECIPE_IMPORT` reservation (premium-only; refunded on any failure). `VideoRecipeService.extract` (below) reads the video's words; the result is sanitized and returned as `{ via: 'video', draft, notFound, unverifiedQuantities, assumptions, transcriptSource, safety, platform, sourceUrl, ogImageUrl, videoTitle, creator, resolution, nutritionStatus }` (the draft's `nutritionInfo` computed from the catalog, as above). `notFound` (`name`/`ingredients`/`instructions`/`servings`/`time`) and `unverifiedQuantities` are decided **deterministically from the source text** (`lib/video-import/text.ts`), never from the model's own claims — it fills servings and times even when nobody said them. `safety` runs the P1-2 matcher over the draft against the household's allergies/restrictions as a warning; no Cheferize call. The client saves the reviewed draft through `save` as the `original` variant. `ogImageUrl` is the YouTube thumbnail only (TikTok/Instagram CDN links are signed and expire).
- **`save(user, input)`** (premium) — re-runs the matcher server-side on any `adapted` payload (rejects violations regardless of what the client sends).
  - **Nutrition is computed on the server** with `RecipeNutritionService.prepareSave`. The client's (and the AI's) numbers are dropped and never stored as USER_ENTERED.
  - Lines may carry the `ingredientId` the review form picked (kept by position through sanitizing), plus `note` and `optional`.
  - `acceptPartial: false` blocks a save whose lines don't all compute (BAD_REQUEST naming them). `true`, or omitted (old clients), saves it PARTIAL.
  - It then creates a `source: MANUAL` recipe with `sourceUrl` provenance and its catalog lines, in one transaction; image = the page's og:image when a guarded HEAD check confirms it serves an image, else the deterministic name-seeded Pollinations URL. Saved imports are rateable/pinnable, so they flow into P1-1 generation placement unchanged.
- Chat tool `importRecipe(url)` (ChatService.buildTools): premium → preview + auto-save (adapted when safe and changed, else original); free → preview summary + upgrade pointer.
- **Friendly AI-failure mapping (§4.5.2):** both AI calls are wrapped with `lib/ai/friendly-error.ts#toFriendlyAiError` — upstream 429/5xx/timeouts become a `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` TRPCError with the "chef is over capacity" copy, other AI failures an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with a task-specific sentence; the raw provider error goes to the server log only (the import sheet used to render the raw 429 JSON blob).

### VideoRecipeService (application layer) — video link → recipe, from its words

`apps/api/src/application/video-import/video-recipe.service.ts`. One pipeline for the in-app import (`recipe.importVideoPreview` → the review form) and the offline CURATED-dataset tool (`pnpm recipes:from-video`). Extraction only — it writes nothing.

**Words only, no Gemini video (owner decision 2026-09-26).** No model ever receives video frames or audio. The transcriber (`lib/video-import/`) turns the link into text, and that text goes through the ordinary text extraction (`IAIService.extractRecipeAnnotated({ text })`, the `importText` route, so any provider — `AI_ROUTE_IMPORT_TEXT`). The annotated prompt's _no invented method_ rule lets a gap come back empty (→ "not found — please add" in the form) instead of as plausible invented steps.

**Transcript pipeline** (`lib/video-import/transcript.ts`, `VideoTranscriber`), cheapest first, stopping at the first source that carries a recipe:

1. **Caption/description** — `yt-dlp --dump-single-json --skip-download` (metadata only). If the caption alone carries a whole recipe (≥3 ingredient-looking lines AND ≥2 method sentences, `captionCarriesRecipe`), nothing else is fetched.
2. **Subtitles / auto-captions** — one track: uploaded subtitles in the video's language (else English, else any), otherwise the ORIGINAL auto-caption track (`*-orig`), never one of YouTube's ~100 machine translations. VTT/SRT flattened, YouTube's rolling duplicate lines removed (`subtitlesToText`). A failure here just moves on.
3. **Speech** — audio only: `yt-dlp -f bestaudio/best` (TikTok/Instagram serve muxed clips; the video track is stripped) → `ffmpeg` to 16 kHz mono 32 kbps mp3 (~0.24 MB/min; Whisper resamples to 16 kHz anyway) → Groq Whisper (`GroqWhisperClient`: `POST {AI_SECONDARY_BASE_URL}/audio/transcriptions`, `model=WHISPER_MODEL`, `response_format=verbose_json`; checked against console.groq.com/docs/speech-to-text 2026-09-26). Segments with `no_speech_prob ≥ 0.6` and the classic "thanks for watching" hallucination are dropped. Skipped when `AI_SECONDARY_API_KEY` is unset.

A caption that carries only part of the recipe (an ingredient list with no method) rides along with steps 2–3, and is used on its own when they come up empty — the form then asks for the rest.

**Caps, timeouts, clean-up, errors.**

- URL allowlist first (`@chefer/utils` `parseVideoUrl`: single YouTube/Shorts, TikTok and Instagram reel/post links only — no channels, playlists or other hosts), and yt-dlp is additionally restricted with `--ies youtube,YoutubeYtBe,TikTok,vm.tiktok,Instagram`, so a URL can never reach its generic extractor (no SSRF surface). The URL always follows `--`.
- `VIDEO_MAX_SECONDS` (default 600) refused from metadata before any download; `--match-filter "!is_live & duration <=? N"` plus ffmpeg `-t N` cover videos with no reported duration. `VIDEO_MAX_DOWNLOAD_MB` (default 50) via `--max-filesize`; the transcoded file must fit Groq's 25 MB.
- Per-step timeouts: probe 45 s, subtitles 45 s, audio download 120 s, ffmpeg 90 s, Whisper 90 s.
- Every temp dir (`chefer-subs-*`, `chefer-audio-*`) is removed in a `finally`. Nothing is stored: audio is deleted right after transcription, and only the text reaches the model.
- `VideoImportError` codes → friendly sentences (`errors.ts`): `UNSUPPORTED_SITE`, `PRIVATE` (login/age wall), `NOT_FOUND`, `BLOCKED` (YouTube's datacenter-IP bot check, 429s), `TOO_LONG`, `TOO_LARGE`, `NO_SPEECH`, `TIMEOUT`, `UNAVAILABLE` (binary missing, Whisper 429/5xx), `FAILED`. The service maps them to `BAD_REQUEST` / `TIMEOUT` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` TRPCErrors carrying only the friendly copy; raw yt-dlp stderr goes to the log.
- **Mock mode:** `AI_MOCK_ENABLED=true` swaps in `MockVideoTranscriber` (no yt-dlp, no Whisper), steered by the URL: `private`, `too-long`, `no-speech` → errors; `caption-only` → ingredient list with no method; `subtitles` → subtitles source; `satay`/`beef`/`no-recipe` → the mock extractor's fixtures.

**Serving-count trust** (`lib/video-import/servings.ts`) — `servings` is the least reliable field and the most damaging when wrong (one clip yielded 2, 3, 5, 5 and 2 across five runs, each reported "high"). When the words state no explicit yield (`serves 4`, `4 servings` — _not_ "per serving"), confidence is capped at `medium` and the form flags servings as "not stated".

**Batch driver:** `scripts/extract-video-recipes.ts` (`pnpm recipes:from-video <url…>` / `--file urls.txt --out drafts.json`) — reports how many drafts came from caption / subtitles / speech. Output carries `stage`, `confidence`, `assumptions`, `sourceText`, `sourceUrl`, `creator`; drafts go to review before promotion to CURATED.

**Legal note.** Downloading from TikTok and Instagram (and YouTube) may conflict with those platforms' terms of service. Chefer only fetches the single link a user explicitly submits (no crawling, no batch fetching from the app), reads the words rather than the footage, stores no media (audio is deleted right after transcription), and saves the result to the user's private collection with the source link. The offline dataset tool is a manual, paced batch (`--delay`). Review this with counsel before promoting video-derived recipes to the shared CURATED pool.

### MealPlanService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/meal-plan/meal-plan.service.ts`. Methods: `generate`, `getActive`, `getForWeek`, `getRecipe`, `swapRecipe`, `replaceRecipe`, `list`, `restore`, `getById` — the plan→DTO join lives once in the private `assemblePlanDto` and week lookups use the indexed `findByWeekStart` (no more 52-plan scans). `getForWeek` carries plans forward: an empty current/next week is materialized as a copy of the user's most recent plan (`findLatestWithDaysBefore`, deliberate write-on-read) and flagged `carriedOver` on that first response — plans continue week to week until the user changes them. Ingredient categorisation is shared: `application/shared/category-map.ts` (word-boundary matching, longest keyword first — "pepperoni" no longer lands in produce via "pepper").

B-13 (T-00.15): `getActive` and `getForWeek`'s offset-0 path used to fall back to `findActiveWithDays` (the newest ACTIVE plan across ANY week) when there was no plan for the requested week — this leaked a later week's plan into "this week" once that week became the sole active plan (every Sunday planner's view). Both now read the new `mealPlanRepository.findForWeek(userId, weekStart)` (same match as `findByWeekStart`, exposed under its own name for these "this week" readers) and never fall back to it; the existing carry-forward (above) is the only other source for an empty week.

B-34/B-46 (T-00.11): `replaceRecipe` runs the picked recipe through `findSafetyIssues(rowToRecipeData(recipe), loadMergedSafety(userId))` before writing the slot. A conflict throws `FORBIDDEN` with a message prefixed `UNSAFE_FOR_TABLE:` naming the allergen/restriction, unless the caller sends `acknowledgeConflict: true` **and** the recipe is the user's own `MANUAL` one (`source === 'MANUAL' && creatorId === userId`) — a curated/AI recipe or someone else's never gets the bypass.

- `generate(userId, weekOffset, premium, options)` — **tier-branched**. **Premium instant path (default since 2026-09-28, `options.instant`, set by the router and the Sunday worker while `AI_PLAN_TAILORING` is on):** `generateInstant` builds the week with the curated builder (`buildCuratedWeek` — the free path's safety filter, shape, keepPinned) plus the premium extras (pinned favourites placed verbatim as `pinned` picks and flags cleared, `pairLeftoverSlots` when `leftovers`, household-sized cost), cancels any RUNNING tailoring of the same week, and — with AI data consent — queues a `MealPlanTailoring` job (`tailoringDayOrder`: today first, past days skipped; Monday first for next week) and returns `tailoring` on the DTO; a pool the curated builder can't cover falls back to the blocking AI week below. `tailorDay` (one day, called by `PlanTailoringService`) reuses `loadPremiumContext` — the exact prompt input, targets and household safety union of the blocking week — then `IAIService.generateMealPlanDay` under a 60 s deadline → `reconcilePlanMacros` → `planOffTargetScore` + one corrective retry when ≥ 15 s remain → `withServerRecipeIds` → `enforcePlanSafety` → `mergeTailoredDay` (locked slots — picks and leftovers pairs — stay; a main the AI left out keeps its curated slot) → upserts the new recipes (image reuse by name, PENDING at the day's priority, `recipeImageWorker.wake()`); it never writes the plan itself. `resumeTailoring` re-queues only untailored days (see §8). `assemblePlanDto` adds `tailoring` from the job row (`toTailoringDto`: CANCELLED or a superseded RUNNING job → omitted; `canResume` computed). The **blocking** path below (`generateBlocking`) remains for `AI_PLAN_TAILORING=false` and pool exhaustion:
  - _Premium_ (or ADMIN): reads prefs **+ learning signals (P1-1)**: pinned favourites (`favouriteRecipeRepository.findPinnedForNextPlan`) and the 20 most recent ratings (`mealRatingRepository.findSignalsForUser`) → **recomputes the daily calorie target live** from body metrics + goal via `computeCalorieTarget` (the stored `dailyCalorieTarget` is a display snapshot and may be stale) → calls `IAIService.generateMealPlan` with liked/disliked dish lines and the daily **macro targets** (protein/carbs/fat from `resolveDailyTargets`) in the prompt → **finishes AI recipes on the ingredient catalog** (`AiRecipeFinisher`, plan-ingredient-catalog §6.3; see below) → one corrective retry when days stray beyond ±15% kcal **or ±20% on any macro** (`planOffTargetScore`, F-PLAN-1-2), keeping the closer attempt → **places pinned favourites verbatim** into matching meal slots (type inferred from the recipe's last appearance in the user's recent plans; pins spread across the week; pinned rows are excluded from the upsert so shared curated rows keep their creator/source) → reuses existing images by recipe name (`findRecipeImagesByNames`) → upserts recipes with `imagePriority` (day-distance from today) → archives old plan → creates new `ACTIVE` plan → `recipeImageWorker.wake()` → clears the `useInNextPlan` flags (a pin means "next plan", not "forever"). The response carries `personalisation { pinnedDishNames, likedCount, dislikedCount }` so the UI can show what the generation learned from.
  - _Free_: `generateCurated` — breakfast/lunch/dinner from the **safety-filtered** curated pool (allergies, dietary restrictions, dislikes — P1-2) for each of 7 days, planned by the pure `curated-planner.ts`: each day picks the combination of the next five unused recipes per type (eight for GAIN_MUSCLE, which also keeps preferring protein-dense dishes once the target is met) that — **portioned** — lands closest to the targets, and adds up to two snacks while the portioned mains still miss (kcal out of ±10% or protein meaningfully short). **Portions (P1-1):** `@chefer/utils` `choosePortions` sizes every slot 0.75×–2× (quarter steps, exhaustive search) so the day lands within ±10% of the calorie target with protein as close to target as the dishes allow (protein-dense meals are upsized first; a cut penalises calorie overshoot). The multiplier is stored on the slot JSON (`portion`, omitted at 1×) and returned as `MealSlotDto.portion`; `recipe.nutritionInfo` stays per ONE serving. A day still short of protein carries `DayPlanDto.proteinGapG` (computed on read for every plan from the portioned totals — under 90% and ≥ 10 g short); the plan also returns `proteinTarget`. A free swap of a portioned slot sizes the new dish to the old slot's calories (nearest step); AI swaps, replacements and rebalance swaps reset the slot to 1× (`updateDayMeal`'s optional `portion`). Everything downstream counts slots at their portion: shopping list lines, plan cost, pantry savings, dashboard planned totals/hero kcal (`nextMeal.portion`), tracker `plannedMeals[].portion` (macros stay per serving; clients default the logged portion to it) and rebalance. Household portions (premium) are a separate factor that multiplies with it. (Audit F-PLAN-1-3 / F-PM-4 / F-TRK-4-2 — days used to land 18–29% under, a 175 g protein target got 43–106 g.) No repeats until a pool is used up, no AI calls, preset images. If any meal type keeps fewer than `MIN_SAFE_POOL_SIZE` safe recipes, throws `PRECONDITION_FAILED` — the meal-plan page renders it as the contextual upgrade prompt.
- **Training days (audit P2-4)** — both tiers call `trainingNutritionService.loadLifter` (constructor-injected) and pass the lifter bodyweight to `resolveDailyTargets` (protein 1.8 g/kg). Premium: the active routine's planned weekdays and the training-day bump go into `MealPlanInput.trainingDays` (`buildTrainingDaysSection` in the prompt, no extra call), and `planOffTargetScore` judges those days against the bumped targets. Free: `planCuratedWeek` gets `trainingDays` and weighs the protein shortfall double on them (higher-protein picks and portions, no kcal bump); the P1-1 portions aim at these lifter-resolved base targets, and plan reads judge `proteinGapG` against them too.
- **Household (F2, premium_plan.md W2-D)** — both tiers load the user's `HouseholdMember` rows (`IHouseholdMemberRepository`, constructor-injected). Premium generation fills `MealPlanInput.householdContext` via `computeHouseholdContext` (portionSum servings, merged safety, per-member dislike notes) and puts the merged allergies/restrictions on the top-level prompt fields; the free curated path, curated swaps and AI swaps run `loadMergedSafety` (union via `mergeHouseholdSafety`, filtering via the unchanged `filterSafeRecipes`) — **safety is never premium**. The pantry context provider (F3) is wired at the marked integration point in `generate` by the wave-2 integrator.
- `swapRecipe(..., premium)` — premium: AI-generated alternative (with name-based image reuse + worker wake); free: random curated recipe of the same meal type from the safety-filtered pool (`PRECONDITION_FAILED` when nothing safe remains). Swap safety uses the household union (F2).
- Per-slot operations (`swapRecipe`, `replaceRecipe`) address a slot through `resolvePlanSlot(plan, dayOfWeek, mealType, slotIndex?)`: the given index (must be a slot of `mealType`, else `BAD_REQUEST`) or, when absent, the first slot of the type. `mealPlanRepository.updateDayMeal(..., portion?, slotIndex?)` rewrites only that one slot — it used to rewrite every slot of the type, so swapping one snack of a two-snack curated day turned both into the same dish.
- `list` / `restore` / `getById` — history + restore support.
- Every assembled `WeekPlanDto` carries `estimatedCost` (P2-4): `application/shared/plan-cost.ts` prices the same aggregated lines as the shopping list (`aggregateIngredientLines`), so the chip equals the list total unless the list adds custom items or subtracts pantry stock. Premium generation feeds `ChefProfile.weeklyBudgetEur` into the prompt as a hard budget constraint; the meal-plan page shows the week cost on every tier and an over-budget warning when the estimate exceeds the budget.
- **Plan shape (§2.3, T-07.1/T-07.2, persona-study wave 1, L-PLAN)** — the "how you cook" settings (which meal types, which days, an optional prep+cook time cap with a weekend exemption, and a "cooking for 1/2" portion) live on `DietaryPreferences` (additive columns from wave 0) and round-trip through the new `PlanShapeService` (`application/meal-plan/plan-shape.service.ts`, `getShape`/`setShape` — `[]` stored `planSlots`/`planDays` is the legacy sentinel, so a user who never opens the settings form keeps today's week, AC7). `generateCurated` loads the stored shape (merged with `generate`'s optional one-off `shape` override), and `curated-planner.ts`'s `planCuratedWeek(pools, targets, random, shape?)` honours it: only the chosen meal types/days are planned (an unplanned day is `meals: []`, `planned: false`); a time cap filters and ranks candidates (known-fast first, then unknown-time ones — owner feedback Q-35: a recipe whose `prepTimeMins + cookTimeMins` is `0` fits any cap but ranks after known-fast recipes); `cookingFor: 2` sets every planned slot's portion to 2 directly (a flat multiplier, separate from the calorie-driven portion and from premium household scaling); an explicit shape without "Snacks" never adds an opportunistic snack (the legacy/no-shape path still does, unchanged); a day that can't fill a wanted slot reports `unfilled: [{ slot, reason: 'time'|'pool' }]` (present on the generation response only — see the read-side limitation note below). The pool-exhaustion check (`PRECONDITION_FAILED`) now only requires `MIN_SAFE_POOL_SIZE` for the meal types the shape actually wants (a "dinners only" shape is no longer blocked by an empty breakfast pool), and attaches a `PoolExhaustedCause` to `error.cause` for T-10.4's machine-readable cause — **handoff request:** `apps/api/src/lib/trpc.ts`'s `errorFormatter` needs a case for it (mirroring `ConflictCause` → `shape.data.conflict`, `lib/conflict.ts` L54-56) before it reaches `shape.data`; that file is owned by a different lane this wave, so the human-readable `message` is unchanged for now (old clients unaffected either way). **Known limitation:** `planned`/`unfilled` are only reliable on the response that generated the plan — a later read (`getForWeek`/`getById`/`getActive`) has no schema column to persist them this wave (schema is frozen for L-PLAN), so `planned` is omitted there rather than guessed; a future wave should add a persisted column if the richer "Not planned" messaging needs to survive a refresh.
- **Pinned slots ("Your pick", T-07.4)** — `replaceRecipe` marks the slot `pinned` (repository `PlanMealSlotJson.pinned?`) and keeps the slot's current portion instead of always resetting to 1× (bug T-BUG-X2/T-08.5); `mealPlan.setSlotPinned` toggles it without touching the recipe. `generate({ keepPinned: true })` looks up the same-week plan being replaced, re-applies its pinned slots (recipe + portion) onto the newly generated week when the day/slot type still exists and the dish still passes `findSafetyIssues`, and reports how many couldn't be kept as `droppedPinned`.
- **Swap/Replace Undo (T-08.5/T-08.6)** — `replaceRecipe`, `swapRecipe` (both the premium AI path and the free curated path) return `previousRecipeId` so the client can implement `Undo` by calling the same mutation back to that id; this wave's default AI-swap behaviour is commit + Undo (no separate preview/`suggestSwap` procedure — Q-6).
- **Regenerate Undo + "What Premium changed" (T-08.3/T-10.7)** — `mealPlanRepository.createPlan` already computed the archived same-week plan's id (`carryFromId`, for shopping-list continuity); it now also returns it as `previousPlanId`, and both `generate` paths (curated and premium) surface it on the response DTO so the client's `Undo` can call the existing `mealPlan.restore({ planId: previousPlanId })` unchanged. A PREMIUM regeneration (one with a `previousPlanId`) additionally computes `premiumChanges { lines[], targetHits, missDays }` — kind-aware lines (training-day bump, leftovers, placed favourites) plus an honest count of days that landed within the existing ±15% day-total kcal band (`PLAN_KCAL_TOLERANCE`).
- **Honest AI-usage counters (T-10.8, bug B-49)** — `reservePlanGeneration(user, premium?)` (`lib/quotas.ts`) now reserves against `AiCallType.MEAL_PLAN` for a premium (AI) generation and the additive `AiCallType.CURATED_PLAN` for a free (curated, zero-AI) one; the free daily cap enforcement is unchanged (same limit number, same serializable-reservation mechanics), but a curated generation no longer inflates the "AI usage" total a future `profile.getAiUsage` change would sum (the `profile.getAiUsage` fields `aiMealPlans`, `curatedPlans` and `importsSaved` landed with L-MONEY on 2026-09-29 — `application/profile/ai-usage.service.ts`, which also marks the day's newest import preview `saved` from `RecipeImportService.save`).

### TrackerService & ScanService (application layer) — F4 Snap-to-Log

`apps/api/src/application/tracker/tracker.service.ts`. Day log CRUD (`getDay` — resolves the day's plan by WEEK (`planForDate` in `meal-plan/plan-for-date.ts` → `findForWeek(monday of the date)`), never `findActiveWithDays`, which returns next week's plan once next week has been opened (UX-FOOD-02; the same resolver backs `upsertDay`, the post-log `maybeRebalance` (current week only, UX-PLAN-09), the coach review's dish names, pantry suggestions and the store-search fallback via `planForThisWeek`); also returns `offPlanLogged` (logged recipes no longer in today's plan; each row carries its `entryId` and `portionMultiplier`, UX-FOOD-03) and `hasActivePlan` (T-19.6: whether the user has an active plan at all, distinct from today just having nothing scheduled — drives the tracker's empty state); `upsertDay` — merges via `merge-log.ts`; `logRecipe`; summaries, weight). Every day write goes through `dailyLogRepository.mutateDay` (serializable transaction + retry, totals recomputed), so concurrent writes never lose entries (audit F-TRK-1-2).
