F4 additions: `logCustomMeal` (appends a custom entry `{ custom: { name, estimatedBy: 'vision'|'manual' }, … }` to the day, portionMultiplier fixed at 1 — macros arrive pre-edited from the confirm sheet), `deleteCustomMeal` (removes one custom entry by its index in the day's `loggedMeals` array; planned entries are rejected), and the `maybeRebalance` hook: after every log write (`upsertDay` and `logCustomMeal` — cook-mode and chat log through these same paths), users with `photoLogging` access get `rebalanceWeek` run against their active plan. Rebalance failures are swallowed (a log save must never fail because of it); mutations return `{ log, rebalance }` so the client can hand applied swaps to the meal-plan banner.

§5.15b (T-19.1–T-19.4, bug B-34, B-23) additions: every `LoggedMealEntry` carries an optional `entryId` (`merge-log.ts`'s `ensureEntryIds`/`needsEntryIdBackfill` — backfilled lazily on read, `getDay` persists the backfill); `updateCustomMeal`/`restoreCustomMeal` edit-by-id and idempotently undo-delete a custom entry (planned entries are still edited by re-ticking a portion); `copyDay` copies every entry from one day onto another with fresh entryIds (dropping the source's `slotIndex`); `deleteEntries` removes any entries (recipe or custom) by a list of stable ids, idempotently — it undoes `copyDay`'s copies via the `copiedEntryIds` it returns; `unlogRecipe` is `logRecipe`'s inverse for the one-save tracker screen (bug B-23): same identity rule (`merge-log.ts`'s `matchesRecipeSlot`, factored out of `logRecipe` so tick and untick can never disagree), a no-op when nothing matches; `recents` returns the last 60 days' distinct logged entries (recipe or normalized custom name), most frequent first, for the search-first Log sheet's "Recent" group (`merge-log.ts`'s `aggregateRecents`). `summary`/`weeklySummary`/`monthlySummary` accept an optional `localDate` (§2.12, T-21.1, bug B-33) to anchor the window on the client's local day instead of the server's UTC one.

`getDay` also runs the §2.11 target-change detection (`targetsService.detectAndRecordChange`, T-11.1) as a best-effort side effect — a broken detection never fails the day read.

`apps/api/src/application/tracker/scan.service.ts`. Backs `POST /api/scan-meal`: `assertMealScanQuota` (FORBIDDEN for free, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS at the matrix limit), writes the `SCAN` AiCallLog row up front (quota counts attempts), then `IAIService.analyzeMealPhoto(base64, mime)` → `{ dishName, confidence low|med|high, kcal, protein, carbs, fat, portionNote }` (Gemini multimodal structured output validated by `parseMealPhotoResponse` in `lib/ai/schemas.ts`; deterministic byte-hash scenario table in mock mode — see MealPlanAIService below). Upstream AI failures are mapped by `lib/ai/friendly-error.ts` to a friendly `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`/`INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` TRPCError (raw error in the server log; scan.router forwards the message as HTTP 503/500). Confirming the estimate is a separate `tracker.logCustomMeal` call — discarded scans never touch the DailyLog.

### Rebalance (application layer) — F4

`apps/api/src/application/meal-plan/rebalance.ts` (the wave-0 seam module — meal-plan.service.ts untouched). `selectRebalanceSwaps` is a pure, fixture-tested greedy selector: project the week (Σ logged kcal Mon…today + Σ planned kcal for days strictly after today) against 7×dailyCalorieTarget; when off by more than ±15%, swap up to 2 FUTURE slots for the curated-pool alternative that most reduces the deviation (safety-filtered pool, no AI call, ≥2%-of-target minimum improvement so re-runs converge to a no-op, stops early once back within tolerance). `rebalanceWeek(userId, planId)` orchestrates: current-week plans only, Sunday no-ops, applies swaps via `mealPlanRepository.updateDayMeal` (by slot index, so each snack of a two-snack day is its own slot) and returns the swaps with an additive `slotIndex` and the previous↔new recipe pairs (+ `planId`) for the client-side undo banner (undo replays `mealPlan.replaceRecipe`; pairs live in localStorage — nothing server-side, wave-0 schema freeze).

### CuratedRecipes (lib)

`apps/api/src/lib/curated-recipes/`. Generic recipe pool for FREE-tier users: the original AI fixtures plus the 42-recipe expansion in `extra-pool.ts` (64 total, ≥3 compliant options per plan meal type for vegan/vegetarian/pescatarian/gluten-free/dairy-free and the major allergens — pinned by `safety.test.ts` and the T-01.1 regression suite below), under deterministic `curated-*` IDs (`source: CURATED`, `imageStatus: DONE`; fixture recipes use stock Unsplash images, expansion recipes use deterministic Pollinations URLs warmed on first use).

**Curated nutrition is computed (plan-ingredient-catalog §6.2, F5).**

- **In memory.** Every fixture line carries its catalog `slug`, plus optional `note` and `optional`. `computed-nutrition.ts` computes each recipe with the shared engine from the committed `catalog.json` (`readCatalogFile`, no database), and `CURATED_POOL_BY_TYPE` serves those numbers. The curated planner, rebalance and Discover therefore read computed values; the fixtures' own `nutritionInfo` is only used by the mock AI provider.
- **In the database.** `ensureCuratedRecipes` then gives every curated row its catalog lines and computed nutrition through `RecipeLineRepository.writeLines`. The fixture is authoritative for CURATED rows; rows already matching are skipped, compared field by field because jsonb reorders keys. If the catalog isn't synced into that database yet, it warns and retries on the next process.
- **The gate.** `curated-nutrition.test.ts` requires all 105 curated recipes (64 original + 15 Romanian staples + 26 diet gap-fill, WP-14) to be COMPUTED, with every slug present in the catalog. `curated-coverage.test.ts` fails if a common diet drops below 10 breakfasts, 10 lunches and 14 dinners.
- **Fixture changes made with this:**
  - "salt and black pepper" and the mixed-berry lines were split;
  - units were moved to portions that exist (an avocado as `piece`, not `medium`), and prep words moved to `note`;
  - a few lines use explicit proxies: halloumi → `cheese-average`, Italian seasoning → `oregano-dried`, fajita seasoning → `chili-powder`, ciabatta roll → `kaiser-roll`;
  - balsamic glaze became balsamic vinegar, and edamame in pods became shelled edamame at half the weight.

**Diet verdicts (UX-REC-01).** `evaluateRestriction(recipe, term, { deriveFromIngredients? })` returns `{ status: pass|fail|unverified, verified, ingredients, reason? }`; `isRecipeSafe`/`findSafetyIssues`/`findSafetyBlockers` take the same options (default strict = tag AND ingredients, the curated pool's fail-safe). Paleo forbids grains/legumes/dairy/refined sugar; keto has a net-carb limit (`KETO_MAX_NET_CARBS_G`) from the recipe's nutrition (`SafetyCheckable` gained optional `nutritionInfo`/`nutritionStatus`) with a staple-pattern fallback; `deriveDietTags` now also derives paleo/keto. `SafetyService.check` adds the optional `taggedOnly` and `conflictDetails` fields to `SafetyChecks` (`@chefer/types`).

`safety.ts` implements the P1-2 filter, made **taxonomy-driven** in T-01.1: pattern tables (`TREE_NUT_PATTERNS`,
`DAIRY_PATTERNS`, …) stay server-side (one enforcement point), keyed by the `patternSet` name each
`packages/types/src/safety-taxonomy.ts` entry names. `isRecipeSafe`/`filterSafeRecipes` match a stored term
literally (unchanged) **and** via `recogniseSafetyTerm` (`@chefer/utils`), so a legacy free-text term — "nuts", "no
eggs", "green vegetables" — expands to its whole pattern set instead of only its own literal substring (C5e,
"interpretation, not rewriting": the stored array itself is never rewritten). Fixes landed this wave:

- **B-02** tree-nut may-contain list: granola, muesli, pesto, praline, marzipan, nut butter/milk join `TREE_NUT_PATTERNS`.
- **B-04** dislike categories expand like allergies (`DISLIKE_PATTERNS`): fish, shellfish, red meat (poultry-exempt),
  mushrooms, leafy greens, onion & garlic, spicy, cilantro.
- **B-03** new `RESTRICTION_RULES`/taxonomy diet keys: `vegetarian-no-eggs`, `egg-free`, `gluten-free-coeliac`.
- **B-47/T-01.9** hidden gluten: `ALWAYS_GLUTEN_INGREDIENTS` (spelt, seitan, semolina, bulgur, couscous, farro, malt,
  barley, rye, regular oats) join `GLUTEN_PATTERNS` outright; `LABEL_DEPENDENT_INGREDIENTS` (stock, curry powder, soy
  sauce, baking powder, oats, chocolate, sausages) surface as `findLabelCaveats()` (`SafetyChecks.labelCaveats`)
  instead of excluding, unless `SafetyPrefs.excludeLabelDependent` (→ `DietaryPreferences.excludeLabelDependent`) is
  set, in which case they exclude — same as the coeliac-strength `gluten-free-coeliac` rule, which always excludes them.
- **T-01.10** `deriveDietTags(recipe)` / `deriveTagQualifiers(recipe)` — ingredient-derived vegan/vegetarian/
  gluten-free/dairy-free tags, independent of the stored (no-longer-trusted) `dietaryTags`; a qualifier is attached
  whenever a derived `gluten-free` tag depends on a label-dependent ingredient (AC14: never a bare tag in that case).
- **T-BUG-51** `findSafetyBlockers(recipe, prefs)` / `describeSafetyBlockers(blockers)` — like `findSafetyIssues` but
  names the actual conflicting INGREDIENT line(s), not just the allergy/diet label, for the import-save rejection copy.

`ensureCuratedRecipes()` idempotently upserts the pool on first free-tier generation; `safeCuratedPools(prefs)` /
`pickRandomCurated(mealType, excludeId?, prefs?)` power filtered generation and swaps. It backs the premium AI safety
pass (`MealPlanService.enforcePlanSafety`), the AI-swap fallback, import validation and the `allergenWarnings` field
on recipe DTOs — and, via `SafetyService` above, every other safety-aware surface.

**Regression suite** (**NEW**, T-01.1): `apps/api/src/application/safety/safety.regression.test.ts` — every curated
recipe × a fixture matrix (every taxonomy allergen/diet/dislike, legacy free-text variants, mixed households) with a
printed per-profile, per-meal-type pool-size report (the B-26 evidence artefact, read from CI logs), plus targeted
acceptance assertions (tree-nut may-contain, dislike-category expansion, the new diet keys, hidden-gluten/coeliac,
label caveats, AC14). §13's CI job now actually runs it (it was a green no-op scaffold before this PR).

### IngredientsService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/ingredients/ingredients.service.ts`. Methods: `search`,
`list`, `catalogList`, `resolve`, `getMany`, `createCustom`, `update`, `delete`, `computeNutrition`, `estimateNutrition`,
`getUnits`.
Powers the create-recipe form, the Ingredients page and the tracker's
search-first Log sheet (T-19.1): catalog search/listing (global + private
custom rows — other users' custom rows are hidden even from admins),
custom-ingredient creation, permissioned edit/delete (owners for custom rows,
admins for global rows; manual edits set `source` USER/ADMIN so the AI
refresher never overwrites them), and server-side nutrition computation (unit
conversion × per-100g macros ÷ servings, with unmatched-name reporting).
`search()` goes through `ingredientPriceRepository.searchCatalog`
(`packages/database`, T-BUG-X7 — it used to query `prisma` directly, skipping
the repository layer) and each result carries `per100g` (calories/protein/
carbs/fat, `null` when the row has no macro data yet) for the Log sheet's
grams row (50/100/150/200 g + live kcal).

**Catalog-backed since P5 (plan-ingredient-catalog §6, §9).** `search`, `resolve`, `getMany`, `createCustom`, `update`, `delete` and `computeNutrition` now read the `Ingredient` catalog through `IngredientRepository`; `list`, `estimateNutrition` and the price consumers still read the legacy `ingredient_prices` vocabulary until later phases move them.

- **Constructor-injected** (`IIngredientRepository`, `IngredientResolver`, `RecipeNutritionService`) for tests against the in-memory `src/test-support/fake-catalog.ts`.
- **`ensurePrivateTwins(userId)`.** Runs before search, resolve and compute. It gives each of the user's pre-catalog custom price rows a private `Ingredient` twin (alias = the name key, `piece` portion from `gramsPerPiece`) and links it (`IngredientPrice.ingredientId`). This is plan §7 step 2, done lazily per user; rows missing a core macro stay unlinked.
- **Legacy `name` field.** It stays a resolvable alias, so old binaries that write free text keep resolving to the same row.

**IngredientResolver** (`ingredient-resolver.ts`, plan §6.1). `resolveMany(lines, ownerId, { candidates? })`:

- **Lookup keys.** Each name's keys come from `ingredientLookupKeys` in @chefer/utils: whole name, then without parentheticals, then before the first comma, then without prep words, each also singularized. They are tried most specific first.
- **Match order within a key:** a global slug (EXACT), then a global alias (ALIAS), then the owner's private alias. All keys go to the database in one query.
- **On a miss:** pg_trgm fuzzy CANDIDATES on `ingredientBaseKey` (top 3). They are suggestions only.
- **Units:** each result carries the canonical unit, the prep `note`, and a `unitProblem` when that unit cannot convert for the match.
- **Ownership:** only rows the owner may see are considered (I4).
- **Shared rules:** the same key rules drive the catalog build's coverage report and the shopping list's `canonicalIngredientName`, so the duplicate normalizer there is gone.

**Weekly review** (`ingredient-review.service.ts` + `src/scripts/ingredients-review-{report,apply}.ts`, plan §8.2, P10). `buildReport(since)` lists the period's ACTIVE private rows (`IngredientRepository.findPrivateForReview`) with the resolver's top-3 global candidates, a per-field nutrition delta, the merge-tolerance verdict and §4.5 sanity flags, plus name clusters across users. `apply(decisions, { dryRun })` runs MAP/PROMOTE through `RecipeNutritionService.relinkIngredient` (recompute with the global row, kcal before/after) and `IngredientRepository.markMerged` (status MERGED, owner aliases and linked price rows move to the global row, one transaction). It refuses merges beyond 25% kcal / 30% macro (floors 15 kcal / 2 g) unless `force`. It writes one `IngredientNotice` per user and review through `IngredientNoticeRepository`. PROMOTE needs the row already synced from catalog.json (D7). Runbook: `docs/runbooks/ingredient-weekly-review.md`.

**Legacy migration** (`legacy-line-policy.ts` + `src/scripts/ingredients-migrate.ts`, plan §7, P8). A one-off, idempotent script. It links global price rows, forces private twins, then plans every non-curated recipe without catalog lines: exact/alias, then `data/ingredients/legacy-mapping.json`, then the legacy unit policy (migration only, never on live saves). It computes through `RecipeNutritionService` and writes through `RecipeLineRepository.writeLines`. The JSON mirror keeps the author's names and units. `ingredients:verify` re-checks I1/I3. Always run `--dry-run` with `--report-dir` first; the report has per-source status counts, the kcal-change distribution by month, and every non-COMPUTED recipe with its lines. `--incomplete` re-plans only recipes that are not COMPUTED (after a catalog change); a legacy "can" line on a cooked legume moves to its canned sibling row. **`ingredients:regenerate`** (`legacy-regenerate.service.ts`, owner decision 2026-10-02) proposes fixes for each still-PARTIAL AI recipe's bad lines through the AI repair round (catalog slug and amount only), skipping lines the legacy mapping left PARTIAL on purpose. A person reviews `regenerate-proposals.json`, and `--apply-fixes FILE` writes exactly those fixes and recomputes, keeping the rest of the dish. Every AI line repair, here and in `AiRecipeFinisher`, passes `repair-guard.ts` (`repairRejection`): no copied counts ("1 head" → 1 g), no look-alike foods, no change of a food the line already named, no amount over 2 kg.

**RecipeNutritionService** (`recipe-nutrition.service.ts`). `compute(lines, ownerId, servings)` runs the shared engine over the rows the owner may see. `recomputeRecipesUsing(ingredientId)` rewrites every recipe with a line on that ingredient through `RecipeLineRepository.writeLines`. A USER_ENTERED recipe whose lines still don't all resolve keeps its typed numbers (D4). Private-ingredient edits trigger it; the recipe write paths adopt it in P6.

**IngredientRepository** (`packages/database`, `ingredient.repository.ts`). Every read is scoped to global rows plus the owner's private rows:

- `findVisibleByIds` returns rows in any status, because lines can point at a DEPRECATED row.
- `findKeyMatches` covers ACTIVE global slugs, global aliases and the owner's aliases.
- `fuzzyCandidates` is a `similarity()` query with bound parameters, the one raw query in the catalog code. It returns `[]` if pg_trgm is missing.
- `searchByAlias` fetches prefix and substring hits separately, so an alphabetical cut-off can't drop prefix matches.
- `findPrivateBySlug`, `createPrivate` and `updatePrivate` write `nutritionSource USER` rows with owner aliases and `user` portions.
- `deprecatePrivate` drops the row's aliases and sets status DEPRECATED.
- `listVisible(ownerId, { key?, text?, category?, mineOnly?, limit, offset })` (P9) pages the ACTIVE rows the owner may see for the Ingredients page: private rows first, then globals by name, `limit + 1` rows to detect `hasMore`. `key` matches any visible alias, `text` the display name. The where-clause is the exported, unit-tested `catalogListWhere`.

`IngredientPriceRepository` gains `findUnlinkedPrivate`, `linkIngredient` and (P9) `findLinkedPrices(ingredientIds, userId)`, the price rows linked to catalog rows that the user may see. `RecipeLineRepository` gains `findRecipesUsingIngredient`.

**`catalogList` (P9, plan §10).** `IngredientsService.catalogList(userId, role, opts)` backs `ingredients.catalogList`, the web Ingredients page. It returns each visible catalog row as a `getMany` detail plus aliases, image and the linked price row, with `editable`: `full` for the caller's private rows, `priceImage` for an admin on a global row with a linked price row (the edit goes through `ingredients.update` by that price row's name, D7), and `none` otherwise. A global row with no linked price row cannot be price-edited until the price worker or the §7 migration links one. The price repository is the fourth constructor argument. `list` (the legacy price vocabulary) stays for installed clients.

**Private-row isolation (plan-ingredient-catalog F6, fixed 2026-10-01):** every
vocabulary load that feeds a user's numbers filters with
`visibleToUser(userId)` (`lib/ingredient-prices`): global rows plus the
caller's own private rows, global only when there is no user. That covers plan
reconcile and swap plus the import cross-check (both through
`application/ingredients/macro-vocabulary.ts` `loadMacroVocabulary`), plan cost
(`estimatePlanCostEur({ userId })`), shopping-list pricing and pantry savings.
Before the fix those loads matched by name only, so one user's private row
could price or reconcile another user's lines.
`private-ingredient-isolation.test.ts` and the shopping-list F6 test run these
paths against an in-memory table (`src/test-support/fake-ingredient-prices.ts`).

### IngredientPriceWorker (worker)

`apps/api/src/workers/ingredient-price.worker.ts`. Builds and maintains the
store-agnostic **ingredient price vocabulary** (`IngredientPrice` table):

- **What it prices** (plan-ingredient-catalog §6.4, F1). On start and every 12 h sweep it collects distinct ingredient names from all recipes and keeps **only names that resolve (exact/alias) to a global catalog row**. Entries that are missing, or older than 7 days, are priced.
- **What it writes.** Every price row is linked to its catalog row (`IngredientPrice.ingredientId`), and existing unlinked rows get linked too.
  - It **never creates a row for a name the catalog doesn't know** and **never asks for or writes nutrition**.
  - `gramsPerPiece`, used for count-unit price conversion, comes from the catalog row's FDC portion (piece → medium → large → small).
- **The AI call.** Prices come from `IAIService.estimateIngredientPrices(names)`, a price-only prompt (`INGREDIENT_PRICES_ONLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, nutrition fields null) in batches of 40. Only the premium private-ingredient auto-fill (`ingredients.estimateNutrition`, D5) passes `{ nutrition: true }`; its result is a labelled suggestion the user edits and owns.
- User custom ingredients (`creatorId` set) are never AI-refreshed.
- The existing rows' old AI macros stay in place, read only by the legacy plan reconcile until P7 replaces it.
- `wake()` — called by ShoppingListService when it serves a list containing
  unpriced ingredients.
- AI out of capacity (429/quota, or the friendly SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE): the
  remaining batches retry after 90 s, doubling per consecutive failure up to
  1 h (`capacityRetryDelayMs`), so an exhausted free daily quota is not
  hammered; a clean pass resets the back-off.

`apps/api/src/lib/ingredient-prices/` converts recipe units (g/kg/ml/tbsp/cup/
piece/clove/…) to the base families and computes per-line price estimates.

### WeeklyPlanWorker (worker)

`apps/api/src/workers/weekly-plan.worker.ts` (PW-5). Hourly tick; on Sundays from 08:00 UTC it pre-generates NEXT week's plan for every `planTier = PREMIUM` user with a complete chef profile (admins get access-premium, not subscriber perks). **Free accounts get a curated week the same way (P2-5)**: `planTier = FREE`, `autoPlanWeekly` on (or no ChefProfile row yet) and a live (unexpired) session, via `generate(userId, 1, false, { origin: WEEKLY_AUTO })` — deterministic, no AI call, no per-user delay; a restriction set that exhausts the curated pool only fails that user. Premium uses `MealPlanService.generate(userId, 1, true, { origin: WEEKLY_AUTO, instant: true })` — the same instant path as the Plan button (a curated week now, tailored Monday-first by `PlanTailoringWorker`; with `AI_PLAN_TAILORING=false` the blocking AI week and the 5 s per-user spacing as before) — so pinned favourites, rating signals, budget and safety prefs all apply (P1-1/P2-4), and the image worker picks the recipes up as usual. Users with `ChefProfile.autoPlanWeekly = false` are skipped. A user who follows a "My weeks" template gets that template applied (`applyTemplateToWeek`, origin TEMPLATE, no AI call) instead of a generated week (F-PLAN-4-1). When a premium generation fails because the AI is out of capacity (`isAiCapacityFailure`), the rest of that tick's premium users are skipped — they still have no plan for next week, so the next hourly tick retries them; free curated weeks carry on. Idempotency comes from the data — a user who already has a plan for next week (`findByWeekStart`) is skipped unless it is an untouched carry-forward copy (origin CARRY_FORWARD with no shopping ticks or custom items, F-PLAN-4-2), so restarts and repeated ticks are safe; per-user failures are logged and don't starve the sweep. Router-level daily generation quotas don't apply to worker calls. The dashboard celebrates the result: `dashboard.summary` returns `weekReady { preparedAt, ratedCount }` only when the active plan's origin is WEEKLY_AUTO (it used to fire for any plan created before its week, including carry-forward copies), and the dashboard shows "Your week is ready — built from N dishes you rated" on Mondays (`ratedCount` is 0 for free accounts: a curated week doesn't learn from ratings).

### PlanTailoringWorker + PlanTailoringService (worker / application layer)

`apps/api/src/workers/plan-tailoring.worker.ts` + `apps/api/src/application/meal-plan/plan-tailoring.service.ts` (pure rules in `plan-tailoring.ts`). Premium "instant week, then the chef tailors it live": generation returns a curated week and queues a `MealPlanTailoring` job; this worker replaces the week's days with AI days, **one day per step, one step at a time across all users** (the free AI tier rate-limits; jobs interleave fairly by `nextRunAt`). Modelled on `RecipeImageWorker`: DB-polled every 5 s, woken immediately when a job is queued (`lib/plan-tailoring-signal.ts` — the service rings it without importing the worker; the pass runs outside the requesting user's AI call context), lease-based claim (150 s, a crashed step's job is picked up again), graceful `stop()` waits for the in-flight day (called in `gracefulShutdown`).

A step (`PlanTailoringService.runNext`): plan no longer ACTIVE → `CANCELLED`; tier or AI consent gone → stop; a new shopping tick since generation → stop; skip (KEPT) days whose JSON no longer matches the generation snapshot or that have a logged meal; `MealPlanService.tailorDay` for the next day; re-check, then compare-and-set write (`replaceDayIfUnchanged`); progress persisted after every day (`currentDay` is written with the lease held so polling clients see it). Capacity/quota errors (`isAiCapacityFailure`) keep the curated day and back off 30 s → 60 s on the same day; other failures (bad output, the 60 s budget) mark the day failed and move on; 3 consecutive failures stop the job. End states: `DONE` (nothing undone), `PARTIAL` (≥ 1 tailored), `FAILED` (none). No per-day AI call logging or quota: one user generation = one reservation, as before.

### WeeklyEmailWorker + WeeklyEmailService (worker / application layer) — P2-5

The outbound retention channel (audit F-PM-14, F-PLAN-4-3), both tiers.
`apps/api/src/workers/weekly-email.worker.ts` ticks hourly and, because no
per-user time zone is stored, uses **fixed UTC hours**: Mondays from 07:00 UTC
→ `weeklyEmailService.sendWeekReady`, Sundays from 17:00 UTC →
`sendWeeklyRecap`. `apps/api/src/application/notifications/weekly-email.service.ts`:

- **Recipients** (`WeeklyEmailRepository.findRecipients`): a confirmed address
  (`emailVerified` set), the matching `User.weeklyEmail*` flag on, and no
  `EmailSend` row for that kind and week. Deleted accounts are hard-deleted,
  so they never match.
- **Monday "week ready"**: this week's plan (skipped when nothing is planned) →
  one dinner per day, the list total from `shoppingListService.getForWeek`
  formatted with `formatMoney` in the user's currency, and a source line —
  premium `WEEKLY_AUTO` = "your chef planned it … N dishes you rated", free
  `WEEKLY_AUTO` = the curated week plus a quiet premium line, `TEMPLATE`, or
  the user's own week.
- **Sunday recap**: meals logged, days within ±10% of the calorie target,
  weight change vs the previous weigh-in, completed workouts (Gym users only),
  next week's planned dinners and the chef-review pointer (premium). Skipped
  when the week has nothing to recap.
- **Idempotency**: `claimSend` inserts the `EmailSend` row _before_ sending
  (`@@unique(userId, kind, weekStart)`); a failed send releases it so a later
  tick retries. 600 ms between sends (Resend's 2 req/s).
- **Daily cap** (`EMAIL_DAILY_CAP`, default 400 for SMTP/Gmail): a sweep's
  budget is `cap − 50` minus every send in the last rolling 24h — weekly
  claims (`WeeklyEmailRepository.countSendsSince`, survives restarts) plus
  this process's password-reset/confirmation sends (`transactionalSendLog`,
  in memory). At the budget, or on a provider sending-limit reply
  (`EmailQuotaError`: Gmail `5.4.5`, `421/454 4.7.x`), the sweep stops
  _before_ claiming — the failed user's claim is released — and returns
  `capped` + `deferred`. The worker re-runs a capped sweep every tick,
  anchored to its original time (a Sunday recap finished on Monday still
  covers Sunday's week), for up to 48 h. Catch-ups live in memory: an API
  restart after the scheduled day drops them (those users miss that one
  email; nobody is emailed twice).
- **Transport** (`lib/email/index.ts`): `EMAIL_PROVIDER` = console mock,
  Resend (HTTP) or SMTP (nodemailer; Gmail + App Password — see §10 "Sending
  email from Gmail"). The sweep uses the raw `emailTransport`; password reset
  and confirmation use `emailService`, which records each send for the budget
  and is never capped.
- Templates: `lib/email/templates.ts` (branded HTML + text part, escaped).
  Every weekly email carries an unsubscribe link and a `List-Unsubscribe`
  header.
- Signed links: `lib/email/tokens.ts` — HMAC-SHA256 over a small JSON payload
  (`EMAIL_TOKEN_SECRET`, else a key derived from `JWT_SECRET`). Unsubscribe
  tokens never expire (scope `WEEK_READY` | `WEEKLY_RECAP` | `ALL`);
  confirmation tokens are bound to the address and last 7 days.
- **Manual trigger** (no procedure):
  `cd apps/api && pnpm exec tsx --env-file=.env src/scripts/send-weekly-emails.ts <ready|recap> [--user=email] [--dry-run]`
  runs one sweep now, ignoring the day and hour but keeping opt-outs,
  confirmation and the send claims.

`EmailPreferencesService` (same folder) backs the `notifications.*`
procedures: the two switches, the confirmation email (sent at signup from
`auth.register`, re-sendable from Preferences) and the public unsubscribe.

### RecipeImageWorker (worker)

`apps/api/src/workers/recipe-image.worker.ts`. Background generator for recipe photos via the configured `IRecipeImageService` (Pollinations by default, Cloudflare Workers AI in prod — see MealPlanAIService "Recipe images"):

- Claims up to **3 PENDING recipes at a time** (atomic per-row claim, horizontal-scale safe) and generates them in parallel, draining the queue until empty; 5 s poll interval is only a discovery fallback.
- `wake()` — called by MealPlanService right after persisting, so generation starts with zero poll delay.
- Queue is ordered by `imagePriority` asc (today's meals first), then `createdAt`.
- Image URLs are deterministic: Pollinations seed + prompt derive from _normalised recipe name + cuisine_ (never the LLM description), so the same dish always maps to the same CDN-cached URL across regenerations. Images render at 512×384.
- **Free fallback instead of "Photo unavailable" (prod incident 2026-09-28).** Every failure path that used to end `FAILED` now ends `DONE` with the recipe's deterministic Pollinations URL (`recipeImageFallbackUrl` in `lib/image-gen/pollinations.ts` = `buildPollinationsUrl(buildRecipeImagePrompt(name, cuisine), name, cuisine)`), and emits the same SSE `DONE` event. The URL is **not** warmed server-side — clients show their "preparing" placeholder until the image loads. Triggers:
  - `ImageQuotaExhaustedError` — Workers AI's daily free allocation is used up (`isDailyQuotaError` in `cloudflare.ts`: error code `3036`/`4006` or the "daily free allocation" wording, any status). The worker then skips Cloudflare **for the rest of that UTC day** (in-memory flag, reset by a restart or at 00:00 UTC), so no more 429 round-trips race the text fallback for neurons. An ordinary 429 is still the short `ImagenRateLimitError` back-off.
  - `ImageStorageError` — the image was generated but could not be stored (local store `mkdir`/`writeFile` failure, unrecognised bytes, Cloudinary upload failure; `CloudflareImageService` wraps any upload failure in it). **Never regenerated** — that would pay again for an image that can't be saved. The worker marks the store broken and serves the fallback without generating until a re-probe (at most once a minute) finds it writable again.
  - The last (`MAX_RETRIES` = 3rd) attempt of any other failure.
  - `ImagenContentFilterError` alone still ends `FAILED` (the prompt itself was refused, and the fallback URL is built from the same prompt). No current provider raises it — only the retired Imagen client did.
- **Startup storage probe** — `start()` calls `probeRecipeImageStorage()` (only for `IMAGE_PROVIDER=cloudflare` + `IMAGE_STORAGE=local`: creates `uploads/recipes`, writes and removes a probe file). If it fails, a loud `✗ IMAGE STORAGE NOT WRITABLE` error names the path and the fix (§12), and generation stays off until the store is writable.
- **Startup backfill** — next to the `GENERATING → PENDING` recovery (same never-crash-boot `try/catch`), `backfillFailedImages()` gives every `imageStatus = FAILED` + `imageUrl IS NULL` recipe its fallback URL and `DONE`, in batches of 100 (max 50 batches), with a per-row `FAILED + null` guard so it is idempotent. Logs the count. Note: a fallback URL is a normal `DONE` image, so MealPlanService's name-based image reuse will reuse it for the same dish later.

### PantryService (application layer) — F3 Zero-Waste Kitchen

`apps/api/src/application/pantry/pantry.service.ts`. The user's kitchen inventory over `IPantryItemRepository` (+ `IMealPlanRepository`, both constructor-injected). Methods: `list` (oldest `updatedAt` first — the use-first order), `seedFromPurchases` (called by ShoppingListService on check-off: upserts PURCHASE rows, normalized names, **staples denylist** in `application/pantry/staples.ts` — salt/pepper/oil/vinegar/water/sugar/dried-spice families are never tracked), `addManual` (premium; rejects staples), `removeItem` (every tier; returns the removed row for Undo), `updateItem` / `restoreItem` (edit amount+unit, Undo — every tier, WP-11 UX-SHOP-05), `markOutOfStock` (the list's one-tap re-add: deletes every row for the ingredient), `confirmWeekly` (v1 depletion: tapped ids deleted, kept rows older than 7 days decay to the "some" state — quantity 0 — with `updatedAt` preserved), `whatCanIMake` (chat tool: ranks active-plan + curated recipes by pantry coverage via the pure `application/pantry/pantry-match.ts`; **B-34/B-46, T-00.11: candidates are safety-filtered first** — `isRecipeSafe` against the user's/household's merged allergies and dietary restrictions — so an unsafe recipe is never ranked, even a perfect pantry match; free tier gets a teaser), and `computeWeekPantrySavings(userId, weekStart)` (Σ estimated EUR of pantry-covered plan lines — the coach writes it into `ChefReview.savedEur` at review time).

**Pantry generation seam** — `apps/api/src/application/pantry/pantry-context.ts` (the provider the household-owned meal-plan loader calls, premium_plan.md §5): `getUseFirstIngredients(userId, limit=5)` returns the top-N OLDEST pantry items in the `MealPlanInput.useFirstIngredients` shape with human `reason` strings; `computeUsedPantryItemsForUser(userId, days)` computes the response `personalisation.usedPantryItems`. `application/pantry/leftovers.ts#pairLeftovers` is the pure "cook once, eat twice" post-processor (pairs 2–3 dinner→next-day-lunch slots, doubled servings, `leftoverOf` labels on the MealSlot Json — no schema change).

### Gym services (application layer) — gym_plan.md §4 (G1-B)

`apps/api/src/application/gym/`. Class services with constructor-injected repositories
(`@chefer/database`: `IExerciseRepository`, `IGymProfileRepository`, `IRoutineRepository`,
`IWorkoutSessionRepository`, `IExerciseProgressionRepository`, `ITrainingPauseRepository`, plus
`IWeightEntryRepository.findInRange` and `IChefProfileRepository.findByUserId` for age). All
progression/weeks/PR/volume logic is the pure engine in `@chefer/utils` (gym) — the services only
load, group, call the engine and persist. `gym-context.ts` loads the per-request context
(equipment inventory, experience, `ageYears` from `ChefProfile.age`, offer state, active
routine); `mappers.ts` owns row ↔ DTO mapping (all dates ISO strings).

- **ExerciseLibraryService** — curated + own custom exercises (archived included, flagged), delta
  by `updatedSince`; custom create/update/archive (owner-only; max 200). Calls
  `ensureExerciseLibrary()` lazily.
- **GymProfileService** — `get`/`save` (partial; a weekly-goal change appends to `goalHistory`
  from the current week; a unit switch with the stock inventory swaps in the new unit's stock
  plates/dumbbells, and any unit or inventory change re-folds every progression via
  `ProgressionService.recompute` so targets are loads the user can make — audit F-GYM-11-2; a
  unit change — and the unit picked in `completeSetup` — is also written to
  `ChefProfile.preferredUnits`, while `syncFromPreferredUnits` applies a global unit change back
  through `save` with `syncPreferences: false`, so Food and Gym share one unit without ping-pong,
  P2-6; `reminderTimes`/`quietNudgeDays` save independently of `reminderTime`/`reminderEnabled`,
  T-36.2), `recommend` (pure engine, no DB: `recommendTemplate`,
  `instantiateTemplate`, `estimateDurationMin`, `volumeByGroup`, `validateRoutine`),
  `completeSetup` (ONE transaction via `gymProfileRepository.completeSetup`: profile with
  unit-appropriate default plates/dumbbells — LB users get native lb plates stored as kg —,
  `goalHistory`, the template routine with `plannedWeekdays` applied as the active routine with the
  pointer on day 1, and an engine `initialState` per (exercise, rep bucket) honouring
  `knownWeightsKg`, which is also kept in `offerState` for recomputes; returns a fresh bootstrap).
- **RoutineService** — list/get/templates, `createFromTemplate`, `createBlank`, `duplicate`,
  `archive`, `setActive` (deactivates the others), `save` (full-document replace in one transaction
  with a `version` check; keeps day/slot ids the client sends back; stale version → `CONFLICT` with
  `error.data.conflict = { kind: 'routine', current: RoutineDto }` via `lib/conflict.ts` +
  the tRPC error formatter), `setNextDay`.
- **WorkoutSessionService** — `upsertMany` (the offline sync endpoint, idempotent; per doc:
  foreign id → `rejected: forbidden`; unknown exercise → `rejected: unknown_exercise:<id>`;
  duplicate ids / bad ranges → `rejected`; older `clientUpdatedAt` → `stale`; same
  `clientUpdatedAt` → `applied` with no write; otherwise upsert row + delete/recreate children; a
  COMPLETED routine session moves `Routine.nextDayId` to engine `nextDayIdAfter` **once**,
  claimed atomically through `rotationAppliedAt`; batch processed oldest-first; afterwards ONE
  progression recompute for every exercise touched, whose failure is logged, not thrown; T-36.3:
  every newly-applied COMPLETED doc also folds `GymProfile.carryOver` through engine
  `nextCarryOver` — consumes exercises the doc addressed, adds `doc.carryOverExerciseIds`
  (`Move them to your next session` / the 24 h save-for-later auto-finish); a write failure is
  logged, not thrown), `get`,
  `list` (cursor `"<startedAt ISO>|<id>"`), `discard`, `delete` (both recompute if the session was
  COMPLETED).
- **ProgressionService** — `recompute(userId, exerciseIds)` (engine `exposuresFromSession` over all
  completed sessions → group by rep bucket → `foldHistory` → persist; buckets that lost their
  exposures fold back to the start; overrides consumed by a newer exposure are cleared),
  `forExercises` (engine `prescribe` for today; exercises without a row get an unpersisted start),
  `setOverride`/`clearOverride`, `startDeload` (7-day window in `offerState`), `dismissOffer`.
- **GymBootstrapService** — the one offline read model: profile, active routine, `nextWorkout`
  (engine `buildNextWorkout` for the pointer's day, passed `GymProfile.carryOver` so it prepends
  any carried-over exercises tagged `fromLastTime`, T-36.3), `carryOver` itself (additive field),
  library (delta + `libraryCursor`),
  progressions with prescriptions, last 12 weeks of completed sessions (engine
  `toSessionSummary`, newest first), `olderBests` (per-exercise max weight / e1RM / Pareto
  frontier of everything before that window, engine `summarizeBests` — live PR badges and the
  summary's PR count seed from it, so a best older than 12 weeks no longer yields false PRs,
  F-GYM-6-1; additive), weeks + streak (engine `summarizeWeeks`), offers (deload via
  `shouldOfferDeload`, stall on `STALL_SUGGEST_SWAP`, comeback after > 8 days, monthly recap on
  days 1–7; dismissals by key), latest bodyweight. `today` is the device-local date from the
  client (server UTC date fallback).
- **GymStatsService** — e1RM series (engine `bestE1rm`; PR flags over all history; 3-session
  rolling-max trend), rep-PR table, weekly muscle volume (`completedSetsByWeek`), consistency, PR
  timeline (`collectPrs`, newest first), monthly recap, bodyweight from `WeightEntry`.
- **TrainingPauseService** — create (≤ 35 days, no overlaps), end (ends today; removes a future one).

### ensureExerciseLibrary (lib)

`apps/api/src/lib/exercise-library/ensure.ts`. Upserts every `EXERCISE_CATALOG` entry by slug,
once per process (shared promise; a failed pass is retried by the next caller). Called at API boot
(`index.ts`, after `listen`) and lazily by the library/routine/profile/bootstrap services. Photo
keys `<slug>-0.3x2.webp` / `<slug>-1.3x2.webp` (T-05.11: an exact 600×400 cover crop, renamed from
the old un-cropped `<slug>-N.webp` so the rename itself bumps `contentVersion` — see
`changedFields` — forcing installed clients' `librarySince` fetch and any URL-keyed cache to pick up
the new crop) are set only for entries with a `freeExerciseDbId` whose file exists under
`apps/api/static/exercises/`, served by Express at `/static/exercises` (7-day cache) and proxied by
Caddy. `ExerciseDto.images` are API-relative paths; clients prefix the API origin.
New catalog entries reach prod on the next deploy through this same boot upsert (idempotent: a
second pass creates/updates nothing). Their photos must be vendored first with
`scripts/gym/vendor-exercise-photos.ts` (free-exercise-db → cover-cropped 600×400 → WebP, skips
existing files); the `ensure.test.ts` "vendored photos" test fails if a catalog id has no files, and
a second test reads every file's WebP header (`webp-dimensions.ts`) to assert it is exactly
600×400. `scripts/gym/exercise-photo-contact-sheet.ts` renders an HTML grid of every vendored photo
for a visual audit; a hit goes in `HIDDEN_EXERCISE_IMAGE_IDS`
(`packages/types/src/gym/exercise-catalog.ts`) and `apps/api/static/exercises/README.md` — `plank`
is the one confirmed so far (free-exercise-db's photo is a lunge stretch, not a plank).
`ExerciseImage` (mobile, `apps/mobile/src/features/gym/components/exercise-image.tsx`) and its web
twin (`apps/web/src/features/gym/library/ExerciseImage.tsx`) show the icon placeholder for a hidden
slug even though the (wrong) file is still served. The catalog has 79 entries (22 dumbbell/
bodyweight home variants added for audit F-GYM-2-1; `incline-barbell-bench-press` and
`back-extension` added for T-05.10, library staples).

### FeedbackService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/feedback/feedback.service.ts`. Beta feedback channel (ux-fixes-plan.md 1.6) over `IFeedbackRepository` (constructor-injected). One method: `submit(userId, message, path?, context?, sender?)` — trims, rejects empty, caps at 2000 chars and stores the row. `context` (`build` / `os` / `route`, UX-PO-05) is folded with the legacy `path` into the `path` column as one `route · os · build` line (≤400 chars; `formatFeedbackContext`) — no schema change. It then mails the owner through an optional constructor-injected `IFeedbackNotifier` (`feedback-notifier.ts`, `EmailFeedbackNotifier` over the existing `IEmailService`; fire-and-forget, failures are logged) addressed by `FEEDBACK_NOTIFY_EMAIL`. The production wiring (repository + notifier + env) lives in `feedback.instance.ts`, so the service's unit tests need no env. Read via Prisma Studio/psql.

### ShoppingListService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/shopping-list/shopping-list.service.ts`. Methods: `getForWeek`, `toggleItems`, `addCustomItems`, `removeCustomItem`, `regenerate`, `searchStores`. `getForWeek`/`regenerate` take the full `UserProfile` — the F3 pantry subtraction is entitlement-shaped.

- **Household scaling (P2-3, F-PM-5):** for premium households (`householdService.scalingPortions`) every recipe's ingredients are multiplied by `portions / recipe.servings` (`shared/household-scale.ts`) before aggregation, ON TOP of the P1-1 slot portion (qty = recipe qty × `slotPortion(slot.portion)` × portions/servings) — a single-portion curated recipe ×portions, a recipe already generated for the table ×1 — and the response carries `portions` (additive). Free households keep recipes as written and get no `portions`; clients never divide a single-portion total by the head count. `MealPlanService` sizes `estimatedCost` the same way (`estimatePlanCostEur(days, { portions })`, which then echoes `portions`), so the plan chip equals the list total.
- `getForWeek` — serves the persisted AI list for the plan when one exists; otherwise builds the categorised ingredient list with the pure `aggregate.ts` (`aggregateIngredientLines`: canonical names, unit-family conversion, water/"to taste"/salt-and-pepper lines dropped; single-source lines keep the historical `name|unit` key so check-offs survive). **Shop-sized lines (WP-11, UX-SHOP-03/04):** `aggregateIngredientLines` first merges citrus zest + juice into whole fruit (`mergeCitrusLines`, `@chefer/utils/purchasable.ts`: per recipe the larger of the two parts, summed across recipes), groups on the catalog `slug` when the recipe line has one (else the name's base key) with unit normalisation from `@chefer/utils/quantity.ts` (`normalizeUnit`: size words large/medium/small/whole/each → `piece`, so "Egg · 4 pcs" and "Eggs · 4 large" are one line), and finally rounds each line to what goes in the basket (`roundToPurchasable`: counts round UP to whole items — 0.8 avocado → 1, 5.5 cloves → 6; a sliver of whole produce written as a weight becomes a count — "Onion 3.2 oz" → 1; weights/volumes round up to a shelf step). The same rounding applies to the pantry's remaining amount and to AI rows. Eggs live in the "Dairy & Eggs" aisle (`category-map.ts`). Persisted AI lists pass through `tidyListItems` and the local aisle map on read. Every item gets an `imageUrl` (resolveIngredientImage) and an `estimatedPriceEur` from the ingredient price vocabulary; the list carries `estimatedTotalEur`. Unpriced ingredients wake the IngredientPriceWorker. **F3 subtraction:** every response carries `pantry { entitled, itemCount, savedEur }`; for `pantryPlanning` accounts, a FULLY-covered derived/AI item gets `pantryCovered: true` ("Have it" chip; never for a line ticked this week), leaves `estimatedTotalEur`, and its estimated price feeds `savedEur` ("saved ~€X this week"); free accounts keep untouched numbers and get the ghost figures only (§6.4). Custom items are never subtracted. **Bug B-24 (T-BUG-24, persona-study wave 1):** a pantry row that covers SOME but not all of a line — previously treated as "not covered" (the whole line stayed, unexplained) — is now a PARTIAL match via the new `buildPantryCoverageMatcher`/`coveredQuantity` (`application/pantry/pantry-match.ts`, `application/shopping-list/aggregate.ts`, additive alongside the unchanged `buildPantryMatcher`/`isShortOf` other callers (`pantry-context.ts`, `pantry.service.ts`) still use): the item stays on the list at its remaining (need − have) `quantity`, its `estimatedPriceEur` scales proportionally, and it gains `haveQuantity?` (the pantry's amount, in the line's unit) so the UI can say "You have {haveQuantity} of {need} · Buy {quantity}". Only applied for `pantryPlanning` (entitled) accounts, matching the existing full-coverage behaviour; free accounts still see untouched numbers.
- `toggleItems(checked: true)` also **seeds the pantry** (F3): the checked items' name/qty/unit are upserted as PURCHASE rows via `PantryService.seedFromPurchases` after the check-off transaction commits (a pantry failure never breaks the check-off); unchecking calls `PantryService.revertPurchases`, which removes the matching PURCHASE rows (MANUAL rows are never touched).
- `addCustomItems` / `removeCustomItem` — user-added items (the page's add-input and the chat's `addToShoppingList` tool) stored in the `customItems` overlay column, so they never shadow the derived list and survive an AI regenerate. Same-name+unit re-add replaces; removal also clears the item's check-off key. Both use the SERIALIZABLE+retry pattern (JSON read-modify-write hazard).
- `regenerate` (premium) — calls the AI to consolidate ingredients and **persists** the result in the `ShoppingList` table (keyed by planId) so it survives reloads. `customItems` and their keys are untouched. Check-offs carry over by canonical ingredient name (`carryCheckedKeys` — regenerating used to wipe every tick, F-SHOP-1-5).
- `toggleItems` and `searchStores` take the full `UserProfile` and read the plan's list lines exactly as `getForWeek` serves them (`listLinesForPlan`: AI rows, or derived lines with slot portions + premium household scale, plus custom items) — pantry seeding gets the quantity the list shows, and the store search gets the aggregated list, not each recipe's ingredients once.
- `searchStores` — delegates to `IGroceryAIService.searchNearbyStores`, passes user's delivery address and currency from ChefProfile. **Dormant**: the store-compare UI was removed from the shopping-list page (store prices come back with per-store price books); the procedure and the grocery-ai/carrefour libs remain for that phase.

### IngredientImageResolver (lib)

`apps/api/src/lib/ingredient-images/index.ts`. Single export: `resolveIngredientImage(name: string): Promise<string>`.

Resolution order:

1. **DB cache** — `IngredientImage` table lookup (instant, zero network cost after first resolution).
2. **Unsplash Search API** — `GET /search/photos?query={name}+food+ingredient` (only if `UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY` is set).
3. **Generated fallback** — deterministic per-ingredient Pollinations product shot (keyless; replaced the old shared category images, prod-followups #6).

The cache persists whatever resolved first, so bad first resolutions stick. The 2026-08-23 catalog audit ([`docs/ingredient-catalog-audit.md`](./docs/ingredient-catalog-audit.md)) found ~90 mismatched rows (wrong Unsplash top hits + dev's legacy shared fallbacks) and repaired them with the one-time `scripts/fix-ingredient-images.ts` (emits idempotent SQL that overwrites flagged names with the generated product shot — overwrite, not delete, because a present Unsplash key would re-fetch the same wrong hit). Macros were audited in the same pass: healthy, no corrections needed.

The Unsplash API is called at most once per unique ingredient name ever seen. All results are persisted in `ingredient_images`.

### RecipeService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/recipe/recipe.service.ts`. Methods: `list`, `discover`, `create`, `update`, `getMyRecipe`, `deleteMine`, `restoreMine`, `isSaved`, `toggleFavourite`, `toggleUseInNextPlan`, `rate`, `getMyRating`.

- **`create` and `update` compute nutrition on the server** (plan-ingredient-catalog §6.2, D4). `RecipeNutritionService.prepareSave` resolves each line: the picked `ingredientId`, else the name exact/alias. Then:
  - every line resolves → COMPUTED; the client's numbers are ignored;
  - some line doesn't, and an old client (no ids) typed its numbers by hand (`source` not `computed`/`none`, kcal > 0) → those numbers are kept as USER_ENTERED;
  - otherwise → PARTIAL with the computed part.

  Lines are stored with canonical units, with prep text moved to `note`; the Json mirror keeps exactly what was typed. The recipe and its lines are written in one transaction (`createManualRecipe` / `updateManualRecipe` with `ManualRecipeLines`). The response adds `lines[]` (`{ position, name, ingredientId, grams, problem? }`).

- **`getMyRecipe`** adds the stored `lines[]` (`grams` null means no data).
- **`deleteMine` / `restoreMine`** (UX-REC-04) — soft delete and its Undo via `softDeleteManualRecipe` / `restoreManualRecipe`; see "Recipe soft delete" in §6. Both answer `NOT_FOUND` for an id that is not the caller's own (or already deleted / not deleted), so ids cannot be probed.
- **`list` paging** (UX-REC-05) — the cursor is the id of the last recipe returned. The Saved tab pages on the `(userId, recipeId)` key (it used to page on the favourite row's id, which a client never has).
- **Copies.** `RecipeCopyService` recomputes a new "Add to my week" copy's lines for the viewer (`copyLinesForViewer`): links to the source author's private rows are dropped (I3/I4), and a USER_ENTERED source keeps its typed numbers unless the copy computes fully.

- `discover` — Cookbook → Discover (P2-8, F-REC-1-4). Upserts the curated pool (`ensureCuratedRecipes`), filters it with `safeCuratedPools` over the owner's safety prefs merged with household members' (`mergeHouseholdSafety`), then applies the pure `selectDiscoverRecipes` (`discover.ts`: meal type, every-word search over name/cuisine/tags/ingredients, prep + cook ceiling, one row per recipe).
- `list({ forTable? })` — B-34/B-46 (T-00.11): when `forTable` is true, rows unsafe for the merged household safety are dropped (`isRecipeSafe`, `hasSafetyPrefs` short-circuits when there are no prefs) — used by the meal-plan Replace picker so it never even lists a recipe it would go on to reject.

- `rate` — upserts a `MealRating` row (1–5 stars + optional notes).
- `getMyRating` — fetches the user's rating for a given recipe.

### DashboardService (application layer)

`apps/api/src/application/dashboard/dashboard.service.ts`. Method: `summary`.
Aggregates active meal plan, today's meals, recent favourites for the Today page (web `/dashboard`, mobile Today tab). The next meal comes from `resolveTodayMeals` in `@chefer/utils`, which skips meals already logged today (F-PM-10); `nextMeal.recipe.cookTimeMins` is additive.
Takes the viewer (`UserProfile`) for the tier-gated training-day bump
(`PLAN_FEATURES.trainingNutrition`, audit P2-4).
B-13 (T-00.15): the week's plan comes from `mealPlanRepository.findForWeek(userId, thisWeekMonday)`, not `findActiveWithDays` (which could return a different week's plan). `showNutritionCards` (B-31 interim, T-00.12) is `chefProfile?.goal != null || dailyLogRepository.findLastN(userId, 7).length >= 3`.

§2.4, T-04.1/T-04.2 (rev 2): `showNutrition` layers `chefProfile.showNutritionOnToday` (an explicit override, either direction) over that same derivation; `jobs` is `effectiveJobs()` over the stored jobs/intent plus the same 7-day log count (TRACK inference). The opt-in `include` reads — `tonight`/`tomorrow` (today's/tomorrow's dinner-aware hero, `done` via `isSlotEaten` from `@chefer/utils`), `shopDue` (via `ShoppingListService.getForWeek`, a **dynamic** `import()` inside the method rather than a top-level one — that service pulls in the AI module, which validates its env vars at import time, and several dashboard unit tests import pure helpers from this file with zero env/DB mocking), `safetyChecks` (via `SafetyService.getTable`/`.check`, read-only, T-11 placement — decorated onto the response only, never written into the stored plan JSON), and `targets` (`planVsTarget` from the already-resolved targets/plannedKcal; `pendingTargetChange` via `TargetsService.listMyUnresolvedChanges`, also a dynamic import for the same env-validation reason).

### TrainingNutritionService (application layer) — audit P2-4

`apps/api/src/application/training-nutrition/training-nutrition.service.ts`.
Read-only bridge from the gym to the food side; the rules are pure functions in
`@chefer/utils` (`training-nutrition.ts`). Constructor-injected repositories
(`gymProfile`, `weightEntry`, `routine`, `workoutSession`, `trainingPause`).

- `loadLifter(userId, chefProfile)` → `{ lifterBodyweightKg }` — non-null only
  for a set-up gym profile + a goal with a g/kg rule + known bodyweight (latest
  weight log, else the profile). Users without a goal skip the reads. Passed to
  `resolveDailyTargets(profile, lifterBodyweightKg)` (protein by goal: GAIN 1.8,
  LOSE 2.0, MAINTAIN / EAT_HEALTHIER 1.6 g/kg) by the dashboard, tracker, chat
  context, coach review and both meal-plan generation paths.
- `targetsForDay(userId, profile, { localDate, weekday }, access)` →
  `{ targets, training }` — base targets plus the training-day payload
  (applied when `access`, previewed otherwise). Read by `dashboard.summary`
  and `tracker.getDay` so both show the same numbers;
  `trainingDayFields(training)` shapes the additive response fields.
  **The bump gate (UX-06, T-06.1, D-2):** callers pass `access` =
  `hasFeature(viewer, 'trainingDayTargets')` (premium-only in
  `PLAN_FEATURES`; the dashboard reads `trainingDayTargets`, the tracker still
  passes `trainingNutrition`, identical for both tiers); the service ORs the
  server flag `trainingBumpFree` onto it (`bumpFlag`, lazy `lib/flags` import
  so pure unit tests never load env), so the flag opens the bump to free
  users at every call site. `trainingNutrition` now means only "build the
  week around training days". **Q-3 (owner decision 2026-09-30): no widening.**
  `hasTrainingDayBump(goal, kind)` is true for GAIN_MUSCLE lift days only;
  `run` / `long_run` days are markers (glyph, header, Explain) and
  `trainingDayBonus` returns zero for them — they never change targets.
- `trainingWeek(userId, profile, weekStart, access, utc?)` →
  `{ trainingDays: PlanTrainingDay[], basis }` (UX-06, T-06.2) — one entry per
  weekday that is a lift day (routine weekday or a completed workout that
  date) or a user-set `run` / `long_run` kind (`ChefProfile.trainingDayKinds`,
  read through `TrainingDaysService.getDayKinds`); each with `kind`,
  `workoutName`, the kind's bump, `done`, `applied`, `targetKcal?`,
  `targetProteinG?` and, for a long run, `preRunSnack` (the evening-before
  carb snack idea, shown on the previous day). Markers are universal (every
  tier and goal); numbers are zero where the goal gets no bump. Backs
  `mealPlan.*` `trainingDays` / `trainingBasis` and
  `dashboard.summary.weekGlance`.
- `refuelSnacks(prefs, count = 2)` → `RefuelSnackDto[]` (T-06.3) — the curated
  `PROTEIN_SNACKS` (`@chefer/utils` `protein-snacks.ts`, each with ingredient
  names and honest diet tags) run through the one safety filter
  (`isRecipeSafe`, owner + household union): no yogurt for a dairy allergy, no
  eggs for egg-free.
- `isBumpWidened()` — whether `trainingBumpFree` is on (D-2 free access; Q-3 widening was declined).
- `previewTargets(userId, metrics)` → `MacroTargets & { lifter }` — backs
  `preferences.computeTargets` (the preferences-form macro preview): the goal
  split for the typed metrics, with the lifter protein rule applied (and
  `lifter: { bodyweightKg, proteinGPerKg }` set) when `loadLifter` says the user
  is a lifter. The Adaptive Chef dial is not applied.
- `trainingSchedule(userId)` → the active routine's `{ plannedWeekday, name }`.
- `trainingDayFor(userId, localDate, weekday)` → completed workout that day
  (a `lift`), else a routine day planned for that weekday, else a user-set
  run kind, all outside a training pause; the result carries `kind`.

### AI recipes on the catalog (plan-ingredient-catalog §6.3, P7)

The model never states nutrition. Generated recipes (week, day tailoring, AI swap) name every ingredient by catalog **slug**, with a quantity in g or ml; the server computes everything.

- **Prompt.**
  - `aiInput.catalogSlugs` / `SwapInput.catalogSlugs` carry `catalogSlugList(prefs)` from `application/meal-plan/ai-recipe-catalog.ts`. It is every catalog slug grouped by category, minus rows that a single ingredient of would fail the table's allergies or restrictions (the same `isRecipeSafe` matcher), at about 3.4k–5k tokens and cached per preference set. It goes first in the user message, so equal lists share a prompt prefix.
  - The rules require exact slugs, raw/dry states for meat, grains and legumes (D8), g for solids, ml for liquids, and no nutrition.
  - `generatedRecipeSchema` (zod) plus the Gemini `RECIPE_SCHEMA` and OpenAI `RECIPE_SHAPE`/`RECIPE_JSON_SCHEMA` have no `nutritionInfo` and a `slug` on every line. Extraction and Cheferize schemas are unchanged.
- **`AiRecipeFinisher`** (`ai-recipe-finisher.ts`, injected into `MealPlanService`):
  1. **Compute** each AI recipe from `catalog.json` (`computeAiRecipe`). A bad slug is fixed only by an EXACT/ALIAS name match.
  2. **One repair round** for every remaining problem line of the plan: `IAIService.repairRecipeLines`, with the resolver's top-3 global candidates.
  3. **Regenerate** a still-broken slot once (`generateRecipeSwap`), then **fall back** to a safe curated recipe, or drop the slot. An AI recipe is never stored PARTIAL. Live tailoring skips the extra AI calls when its deadline is near (`canCallAi`).
  4. **Fit** each AI recipe to its slot's share of the day target (`slotTargets`: breakfast 22.5 / lunch 32.5 / dinner 37.5 / snack 12.5 %, normalised over the day's meals; training-day targets included). When it is outside ±10%, every quantity is scaled by target/computed, clamped 0.6–1.8×, rounded (`roundQuantity`) and recomputed.
  5. After the row upsert, **`persistLines`** writes the recipe's catalog lines (status COMPUTED) through `RecipeLineRepository.writeLines`.

  An AI swap is fitted to the computed kcal of the dish it replaces; a swap that still won't compute falls back to curated.

- **Afterwards.** Day-total validation and its one corrective retry (`planOffTargetScore`) are unchanged but now read computed numbers.
- **Removed.** The old `macro-reconcile` rescaling toward the AI's stated calories and the AI-macro vocabulary loader are gone; `macro-reconcile.ts` keeps only `roundQuantity`.
- **Eval.** `scoreMealPlan` computes day kcal and macros from slugs and adds `checks.catalogResolution`, the share of lines resolved without repair (target ≥ 0.95). Run it with `pnpm ai:eval --provider=mock` for free; live providers cost real calls.

**Recipe images** sit behind `IRecipeImageService` (`lib/image-gen/`): `IMAGE_PROVIDER=pollinations` (default, anonymous URL) or `cloudflare` (`CloudflareImageService`: Workers AI `CF_IMAGE_MODEL`, default flux-1-schnell). Cloudflare bytes go through `lib/image-cdn/local.ts` (`createLocalImageStore`) into `uploads/recipes/<recipeId>-<sha256:12>.<ext>` — the same `uploads` volume and `/uploads/*` static route as user photos — and the stored URL is `API_PUBLIC_URL`/`APP_URL` + `/uploads/recipes/…`. The file type is sniffed from the bytes; the content hash in the name keeps the `immutable` cache honest when an image is regenerated. `IMAGE_STORAGE=cloudinary` switches to the optional Cloudinary upload instead. The recipe-image worker calls `generateAndUploadRecipeImage` (plus `probeRecipeImageStorage` at startup and `recipeImageFallbackUrl` for the free fallback). Error contract (`lib/image-gen/errors.ts`): `ImagenRateLimitError` = short back-off, `ImageQuotaExhaustedError` = daily free allocation gone, `ImageStorageError` = generated but not stored (never regenerate), `ImagenContentFilterError` = permanent — see RecipeImageWorker.

**Free-only mode:** `AI_FREE_ONLY=true` runs every workload on `groq>cloudflare` (Groq free tier, then Workers AI's free 10K neurons/day), with no Gemini at all; see `docs/ai-providers.md` "Free-only mode" for the exact lines and capacity maths.

**Switching providers:** `AI_PROVIDER=gemini` (+ `GEMINI_API_KEY`) makes `gemini` available; `AI_SECONDARY_API_KEY` makes `groq` (the OpenAI-compatible secondary) available. Each workload then follows its `AI_ROUTE_*` chain (unset = today's table: plan/swap/cheferize/text import/review `gemini>groq`; chat/prices/shopping `groq>gemini`; vision `gemini`). `AI_PROVIDER=openai` runs the secondary alone for every workload (photos use `AI_VISION_MODEL`, plans are chunked, `GEMINI_API_KEY` is not required); the exact Groq-only production lines are in `docs/ai-providers.md` "Running without Gemini". The runbook for moving a workload off Gemini (eval → a week of shadow → flip) is `docs/ai-providers.md`. No code changes required.

**Mock steering conventions (premium_plan.md §4.5):** with no steering keyword every method returns its frozen default (byte-identical to wave 1), so existing tests and dev flows never change; keywords only ADD reachable scenarios so every AI branch can be driven without live Gemini calls (the shared key is free-tier, 20 requests/day):

| Method                | Steering                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extractRecipe`       | Keyed off the source url/text (case-insensitive): `satay`/`peanut` → allergen-bearing chicken-satay fixture; `unsafe` → the satay fixture with the `UNSAFE` magic name; `beef` → beef-steak fixture; `no-recipe` → `NO_RECIPE_FOUND` sentinel; else the default pasta (photo sources too)    |
| `cheferizeRecipe`     | Real deterministic adapter: substitution map + serving rescale + accurate `changes[]`, swapped terms also removed from the dish name. A recipe whose ORIGINAL name contains `UNSAFE` skips the swaps — the P1-2 matcher then fails the adaptation closed (drivable from the import UI)       |
| `analyzeMealPhoto`    | Scenario table indexed by `imageBase64.length % 5` (base64 lengths are multiples of 4, so padding a file by 3 raw bytes shifts the residue by −1). Index 0 = the wave-1 default (520 kcal, med); index 4 = the ~2310 kcal feast that trips the ±15% rebalance threshold; covers low/med/high |
| `generateMealPlanDay` | Live tailoring: the fixture week's day for `dayOfWeek` (with the same seam handling), cloned. Like `generateMealPlan`, delayed by `AI_MOCK_DELAY_MS` on top of its base delay so tailoring progress can be watched locally                                                                   |

### RecipeLineRepository (infrastructure layer) — ingredient catalog

`packages/database/src/repositories/recipe-line.repository.ts` (plan-ingredient-catalog §3). `writeLines(recipeId,
lines, nutrition, tx?)` replaces a recipe's `RecipeIngredient` rows and rewrites its `ingredients` Json mirror
(`{name, quantity, unit}`, `mirrorName ?? rawName` per line), `nutritionInfo` (rounded per serving), `nutritionTotal`,
`nutritionStatus` and `nutritionComputedAt` (null for `USER_ENTERED`) in ONE transaction, or inside the caller's `tx`.
It is the only write path for lines, so rows, mirror and nutrition never disagree; `upsertRecipes` never updates
ingredients or nutrition on an existing id (F10); for CURATED rows it does update `servings`, because the fixture is authoritative and their lines are computed per fixture serving. `findByRecipeIds` reads lines ordered by recipe and position. Pure
helpers `toIngredientsMirror`, `toLineRows` and `toNutritionColumns` are exported for tests and scripts.

Implements `IUserRepository` from `@chefer/database`. Lives in `apps/api/src/infrastructure/prisma/`.

### SafetyService (application layer) — T-01.1/T-01.2, the ONE safety filter

`apps/api/src/application/safety/safety.service.ts`. Every safety-aware surface starts from
`SafetyService.loadContext(userId)`: owner + household `DietaryPreferences`/`HouseholdMember` rows, merged (hard
union — allergies, dietary restrictions AND, since T-01.2, dislikes: owner decision 2026-09-27), plus this user's
reported recipe ids (UX-01 d). Methods:

- `loadContext(userId): SafetyContext` — `{ prefs: SafetyPrefs, hiddenRecipeIds: string[], table: TableSafety }`.
- `getTable(userId): TableSafety` — the read-back shape (`safety.getTable`), each stored term run through
  `recogniseSafetyTerm` (`@chefer/utils`) so legacy free text ("nuts", "no eggs") reads as its canonical label; a
  condition with no safe automatic reading (anything but coeliac) becomes a `notes` entry instead of an `items` row.
- `check(recipe, table): SafetyChecks` — `{ checked: {label,who}[], conflicts: string[], unchecked: string[],
labelCaveats?: {ingredient,rule}[] }` — one recipe against the whole table, per-person attribution.
- `filter(pool, ctx, opts?): T[]` — the pool minus unsafe rows and reported rows; `opts.dislikes: 'mark'` (search
  surfaces, UX-01) skips the dislike exclusion so the caller can chip it instead of hard-hiding it. `T` only needs
  `RecipeSafetyLike` shape (works directly on a raw Prisma `Recipe` row, no reshaping).
- `decorate(recipe): T & { derivedTags, tagQualifiers? }` — T-01.10: ingredient-derived diet tags
  (`deriveDietTags`/`deriveTagQualifiers` in `curated-recipes/safety.ts`) — the curated pool's static `dietaryTags`
  are no longer trusted for gluten-free/vegan/vegetarian/dairy-free. **Wave 2 (L-SAFE2, T-01.10/T-02.1):** called from
  `meal-plan.service.ts`'s two recipe-DTO mappings (`rowToRecipeDto`/`toRecipeDto` callers) via the shared
  `decorateRecipeDto` helper — every plan-surface recipe now carries `derivedTags`/`tagQualifiers?` alongside
  `allergenWarnings?`/`safetyChecks?` (see `mealPlan.getById` below).
- `report(userId, input)` / `listMyReports(userId)` / `confirmReview(userId)` back `safety.report` / `safety.myReports`
  / `safety.confirmReview` (§8).

The matcher itself stays one module, `apps/api/src/lib/curated-recipes/safety.ts` — see the **CuratedRecipes**
section below for T-01.1's taxonomy-driven pattern tables. Wired into: `RecipeService.list({forTable})` /
`.discover`, `PantryService.whatCanIMake`, `RecipeImportService` (preview + `importSave` BOTH variants — T-BUG-X3),
`rebalanceWeek` (T-BUG-X1). T-02.3/T-02.5 add two more callers, both read-only and additive:
`RecipeService.getSafetyChecks` (`check()` against a single recipe, §8 `recipe.getSafetyChecks`) and
`RecipeService.discoverHiddenCount` (diffs a `safeCuratedPools(null)` pass against a `safeCuratedPools(prefs)` pass,
§8 `recipe.discoverHiddenCount`). **Not wired** (outside L-SAFE's file ownership this wave — recorded as a handoff
request): `ChatService.buildContextSummary` still reads only the owner's `DietaryPreferences` (T-BUG-X1's chat half).

**Wave 2 (L-SAFE2, T-02.1/T-01.5/T-01.9, business_flow.md §27):** `MealPlanService` (`meal-plan.service.ts`) now
loads its safety context via `SafetyService.loadContext` instead of a locally re-merged copy
(`loadSafetyContext`/former `loadMergedSafety`) — every plan read (`assemblePlanDto`, `buildCuratedWeek`'s and
`generateBlocking`'s own inline DTOs, `planDay`), `getRecipe`, `swapRecipe`/`swapCurated` and `replaceRecipe` attach
`safetyChecks?`/`derivedTags`/`tagQualifiers?` (and, for `getById`/`getForWeek`/`getActive`/`generate`/`restore`, a
top-level `tableSafety?`) via the shared `decorateRecipeDto` helper. Reported recipes (T-01.5) are excluded from the
curated pool everywhere it's drawn from — `buildCuratedWeek`, `planDay`, `swapCurated` and `enforcePlanSafety`'s
unsafe-AI-slot replacement (so a reported recipe never resurfaces in a fresh instant/curated week **or** a later
live-tailored day, `tailorDay` → `enforcePlanSafety`) — via a local `pickSafeCurated` wrapper around
`pickRandomCurated` that also filters `hiddenRecipeIds` (falls back to the unwrapped shared helper when there is
nothing to exclude, so the common no-reports path is unchanged). `RecipeService.list({ forTable: true })` and
`.discover` now also attach `safetyChecks?` per row; NEW `recipe.listHiddenCount` mirrors `discoverHiddenCount` for
the Replace picker (§8). `ShoppingListService.getForWeek` attaches a top-level `tableSafety?` and, per item,
`labelCheck?: string[]` (T-01.9) for label-dependent ingredients (`LABEL_DEPENDENT_INGREDIENTS`) when the table has a
gluten-free diet. Safety decoration is read-only everywhere — it is never written into a plan's stored day JSON, so
it cannot interfere with `plan-tailoring.service.ts`'s compare-and-set (`isTouched`/`replaceDayIfUnchanged`).

### AI-consent gate (lib layer) — R-10, App Store 5.1.2(i)

`apps/api/src/lib/ai-consent-gate.ts`. The server-side half of the AI-data consent: `aiConsentMissing({ userId, mode? })` (enforcement on AND `userRepository.findAiDataConsentAt` is null), `assertAiConsent` (throws `aiConsentRequiredError()`: FORBIDDEN, `AiConsentRequiredCause`), `rejectWithoutAiConsent(res, …)` (Express 403 + `reason` + `X-AI-Consent-Required`). Mode = `env.AI_CONSENT_ENFORCE`, imported lazily (a bare unit test without the secret set means `off`; the shipped default `on` lives in `env.ts`). `lib/trpc.ts` wraps it as `requireAiConsent(appliesTo?)` and `aiConsentProcedure`; see §9 for the full list of gated procedures. `MealPlanService.generate` / `generateInstant` call `aiConsentMissing` to degrade to the curated week instead of the blocking AI week. Background jobs are unchanged and already respect consent (`WeeklyPlanWorker`, `PlanTailoringService`, `CoachService.runReviewSweep`); `IngredientPriceWorker` only sends the global catalog vocabulary.

### ConsentService (application layer) — the single consent-log write path (T-39.2)

`apps/api/src/application/privacy/consent.service.ts`. `record({ userId, kind, granted, source, documentVersion?, providers? })` appends one `ConsentEvent` (never updates/deletes); `history(userId)` and `latest(userId, kind)` read it back. Every consent writer calls this instead of touching `consentEventRepository` directly, so the log is 100% complete:

- `UserService.setAiDataConsent` (grant/revoke AI, kind `AI`) — only on a real transition, so a double-tap doesn't double-log.
- `EmailPreferencesService.set` (kind `EMAIL_WEEK_READY` / `EMAIL_RECAP`) — one row per switch actually present in the call.
- `PrivacyService.recordAnalyticsConsent` (kind `ANALYTICS_ANON` / `ANALYTICS_LINKED`, T-12.3) and `PrivacyService.acceptTerms` (kind `TERMS` + `PRIVACY`, + `AGE` when given, T-39.2) both build on it.
- Also called (other lanes' branches, same stable signature): L-ENTRY's `auth.register` (`TERMS`/`PRIVACY`/`AGE` at sign-up), L-TRACK's `preferences.setAutoPlanWeekly` (kind `AUTO_PLAN`).
  `source` is always `ctx.isMobileClient ? 'mobile' : 'web'` at the router, never a client-supplied field — `recordAnalyticsConsent`'s input is `{ anonymous?, linked? }` only.

### TargetsService (application layer) — §2.11, T-35.1/T-11.1/T-35.4

`apps/api/src/application/targets/targets.service.ts`. The `targets.*` procedures: reads the resolved view (recomputing and detecting a silent change on every read), lets a user set their own override, and resolves a detected/proposed change.

- **`get(userId)`** — `resolveTargets` (see `PreferencesService` below) + own-target state (`targetMode`, `custom.{kcal,proteinG,carbsG,fatG,trainingKcal,trainingProteinG}`, `addTrainingBonus`). As a side effect, calls `detectAndRecordChange`.
- **`set(userId, user, input)`** — sets or clears the own-target override. Gated by the `ownTargetsFree` flag (default on) for free tier, otherwise `isPremiumUser`. Validates kcal (1,200–5,000), protein (40–400 g), and — when carbs/fat are given — that the macros imply calories within ±10% of the stated kcal (4/4/9 rule). Writes `ChefProfile.{targetMode,customKcal,customProteinG,customCarbsG,customFatG,customTrainingKcal,customTrainingProteinG,addTrainingBonus}` and keeps the legacy `dailyCalorieTarget` in step with the new effective value.
- **`changes(userId)` / `acknowledgeChange(userId, { id, keep })`** — the change log. `keep: true` always means "keep what I already have" (a `CHANGED` row restores the pre-change numbers as an `OWN` override; a `SUGGESTED` row — including the coach's proposal — is declined, nothing moves). `keep: false` means "use the new/suggested value" (a `CHANGED` row's new numbers are already applied, so this just resolves the row; a `SUGGESTED`/`COACH` row applies the proposal to `targetAdjustmentKcal` via `applyCoachProposal`, which looks up the most recent `ChefReview` with an unresolved `proposedAdjustmentKcal`).
- **`detectAndRecordChange(userId, profile, resolved)`** — "never change your targets silently" made provable. Compares the freshly resolved view against `ChefProfile.targetSnapshot` (the last `{ effective, suggested, inputs }` the user saw); when it moved without the user asking, writes a `TargetChange` row (`kind: CHANGED` for a `SUGGESTED`-mode user whose `effective` moved, `kind: SUGGESTED` for an `OWN`-mode user whose `suggested` drifted ≥ 5%), then advances the snapshot. The reason (`GYM_SETUP`/`WEIGHT`/`GOAL`/`DAY_KIND`) is inferred from which `TargetInputs` field changed; weight-driven notices are debounced to one per 7 days. Called by `targets.get` and `tracker.getDay` (both best-effort — a broken detection never fails the read). **Handoff**: `dashboard.summary` (`application/dashboard/**`, owned by L-HOME) should call it too — it doesn't yet.
- **`proposeCoachAdjustment(userId, currentKcal, adjustmentKcal)`** — writes a `SUGGESTED`/`COACH` `TargetChange`. Called by `CoachService.runWeeklyReview` right after it stores `ChefReview.proposedAdjustmentKcal` (T-35.4: the coach proposes, it no longer writes `targetAdjustmentKcal` itself).
  Known gap: `IChefReviewRepository` only exposes `resolveProposal` (sets `proposalResolvedAt`), so `applyCoachProposal` can't also set `ChefReview.adjustmentKcal` to the applied amount — it stays 0 even after acceptance. A `packages/database` follow-up (not owned by this lane) should add that.
  | `TrainingDaysService` (`application/training-days/`, **T-06.9, was `TrainingService` in `application/training/`**) | `getDayKinds(userId)` + `setDayKinds(userId, days)` | `chefProfileRepository` | T-06.10 (kind-led nutrition bumps, `training-nutrition.service.ts`) |

by a service field by field into a `@chefer/types` DTO (INV-2) — never a spread row, never an email (INV-6).

The PRD §7.1 matrix is its test oracle                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Recipe access (`application/recipe/recipe-access.ts`).** `findRecipeVisibleTo`/`isRecipeVisibleTo` keep the old rules
and gain the social branch (§9). `recipeAttribution()` builds the additive `creator` / `origin` / `hidden` keys
(omitted, never `null`, when they don't apply, so a user who never used Following sees today's key set). The branch and
every read of it fail closed. `RecipeService.list` joins hearted originals of followed creators into Saved/All
(`FavouriteRecipeRepository.findAllRecipesForUser` takes `visibleCreatorIds`) and strips the raw Following columns from
its rows. `MealPlanService.assemblePlanDto` drops (and logs) a slot whose recipe row is missing instead of throwing,
because an owner can delete an original that a copy-less plan still names.
